articles.title: Modi in Bengaluru: PM flags off elevated stretch of Namma Metro Pink Line | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The opening of the elevated section of the Pink Line is expected to offer only minor relief to the city’s gridlock, with the crucial underground section connecting the Central Business District to north Bengaluru awaiting completion, writes Darshan Devaiah B.P. Mind the gap: Partial opening of Namma Metro Pink Line leaves commuters wanting Partial opening of Bengaluru's Namma Metro Pink Line offers limited relief; underground North-South link remains pending until 2027.
Partial opening of Bengaluru's Namma Metro Pink Line offers limited relief; underground North-South link remains pending until 2027.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off the elevated section of Bengaluru’s Pink Line Metro at S.G. Palya (Suddagunte Palya) Metro Station, in the presence of Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav and Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar.

The Pink Line is part of Namma Metro’s Phase II and is designed to connect Kalena Agrahara in south Bengaluru with Nagawara in north Bengaluru. The 21.25-km corridor comprises a 7.5-km elevated section and a 13.76-km underground section.
Once fully operational, the corridor is projected to carry approximately 3.76 lakh passengers daily, according to the Detailed Project Report (DPR).

Mr. Modi later travelled by Metro to Bilekahalli-IIMB Metro Station accompanied by Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda and Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya.
Before entering the platform, Mr Modi purchased a Metro ticket. BMRCL officials briefed him on the project before he boarded the train, a BMRCL source told The Hindu .

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav have arrived by helicopter at the R.A. Mundkur Fire and Emergency Services Training Centre campus near Dairy Circle on Bannerghatta Road in Bengaluru.

Modi will proceed to S.G. Palya (Suddagunte Palya) Metro Station, where he, along with Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, will flag off the Pink Line Metro service and undertake a ride to Bilekahalli-IIMB Metro Station.

The PM will also unveil plaques marking the foundation stone-laying of three projects, including a compressed biogas plant at Haralakunte village in Bengaluru South and two power transmission projects.
He will also inaugurate renewable energy transmission schemes in Koppal, Gadag and Bidar.
The programme also includes dedication of an 80 TMT LPG cavern developed by HPCL, the Devangonthi Marketing Terminal of MRPL, railway doubling and electrification projects.

articles.title: Central Railway to run four special Mumbai-Nagpur trains between November 13-15
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Central Railway has announced four special train services between Mumbai and Nagpur from November 13 to 15 to accommodate additional passenger traffic during the festive season.

According to a press release issued on Thursday (November 12, 2026), two services will operate between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) and Nagpur, while two others will run between Lokmanya Tilak Terminus (LTT) and Nagpur.

Train No. 01125 will depart from CSMT at 3.25 p.m. on November 13 and reach Nagpur at 7 a.m. the following day. On its return journey, Train No. 01126 will leave Nagpur at 4.10 p.m. on November 14 and arrive at CSMT at 8.05 a.m. the next day.
The CSMT-Nagpur special will halt at Dadar, Thane, Kalyan, Igatpuri, Nashik Road, Chalisgaon, Jalgaon, Bhusaval, Malkapur, Shegaon, Akola, Badnera, Dhamangaon and Wardha.

Similarly, Train No. 01129 will depart from LTT at 3.25 p.m. on November 14 and reach Nagpur at 7 a.m. the following day. The return service, Train No. 01130, will leave Nagpur at 4.10 p.m. on November 15 and arrive at LTT at 8.05 a.m. the next day.
The LTT-Nagpur special will stop at the same stations as the CSMT service, except Dadar.
Both special trains will have AC, sleeper and general-class coaches.
The CSMT-Nagpur service will also include AC three-tier economy coaches.

Central Railway said bookings for the reserved coaches are open at computerised reservation centres and through the IRCTC website. Tickets for unreserved coaches can be booked through the UTS system or the RailOne app at normal charges.
Passengers can check detailed schedules and stoppage timings through the National Train Enquiry System website or mobile application.

articles.title: Gig and platform workers’ strike call in Hyderabad on November 14, plan major rally
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Gig and platform workers have called for a strike in the city on November 14 to demand social security, workers’ rights, and welfare measures, according to the Telangana Gig and Platform Workers’ Union (TGPWU).

TGPWU office-bearer Shaik Salauddin said on Thursday that Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been invited to join the rally with the union extending gratitude to him for “his advocacy and action for the welfare of gig and platform workers”, especially against the backdrop of the 2023 Bharat Jodo Yatra.

“The Telangana Gig and Platform Workers Act 2026 provides a vital legal framework for worker rights, centered on mandatory registration, social security benefits, a dedicated welfare board, and an effective grievance redressal mechanism. The state government has formulated the rules for implementing the Act, initiating steps to constitute the Welfare Board and launching a dedicated app to register workers and resolve grievances ,” Mr. Salauddin said.

articles.title: Andhra to bring in Investment Protection Act to ease doing business, says Naidu

fullParagraphs: Addressing the inaugural session of the 31st CII Partnership Summit 2026 on Thursday (November 12, 2026), Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu said Andhra Pradesh was working towards becoming a major manufacturing and technology hub in areas such as rare earth minerals, steel production, solar wafers, solar energy and battery energy storage.

He said that Asia’s first 120-qubit quantum computer in Amaravati would be inaugurated on February 3, 2027 and the Google Data Centre in Visakhapatnam on August 15, 2028, and that 303 MoUs involving proposed investments to the tune of ₹9.89 lakh crore would be signed at the ongoing summit. This would take the value of the investment proposals attracted by A.P. since June 2024 to ₹32.49 lakh crore, he said.

He stated that Asia’s first 120 qubit quantum computer in Amaravati would be inaugurated on February 3, 2027 and the Google Data Centre in Visakhapatnam on August 15, 2028, and that 303 MoUs involving proposed investments to the tune of ₹9.89 lakh crore would be signed at the ongoing Summit. With this, the value of the investment proposals attracted by A.P. reached ₹32.49 lakh crore since June 2024.

Emphasising the State’s commitment to speedy clearances, Mr. Naidu said A.P. was granting approvals at a speed that was unmatched by others and it was clear from the record time in which the government had facilitated the establishment of the Kia car manufacturing plant in Sri Sathya Sai district.

The grant of approvals to the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft project which was also coming up in Sri Sathya Sai district was another shining example of the priority attached to speedy clearances. LG Electronics was preparing to commence production in Sri City within 19 months.

The Chief Minister outlined ambitious targets across key sectors: renewable energy 160 GW, annual electronics production ₹4.20 lakh crore, and aerospace and defence sector ₹50,000 crore. He observed that Amaravati was being developed as a blue-green capital city and it offered tremendous opportunities as it was poised to emerge as one of the most livable cities.

Highlighting the State’s strategic geographical advantage, Mr. Naidu said the State was emerging as a leading logistics destination with six operational ports, airports, high-speed rail connectivity and an extensive road network. Comprehensive plans were drawn up to ensure water availability for agriculture, drinking water and industrial requirements through interlinking of rivers, of which the Polavaram project was a major component.

The State government was committed to the Swarna Andhra Vision 2047 and a clear roadmap had been prepared for it, Mr. Naidu said, and called upon global investors, industrialists and technology leaders to partner with the State in realising that vision.

articles.title: The SIR exercise is also a technology failure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Much of the public argument over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of India’s electoral rolls is around law, power and politics. The autonomy of the Election Commission of India (ECI), the list of acceptable documents, and the burden placed on voters to prove eligibility are the key focus issues. There is, of course, no doubt that these questions matter. But a quieter, less spoken-about story runs underneath them. The 2025-26 SIR is the first revision of this scale to be run through a centralised digital platform, and the technology itself has become a source of exclusion. Viewed as a nationwide digital transformation project, the SIR fails on several counts that any student of technology would immediately recognise.

The irony stares right at us. India presents itself, with ample reasons to do so, as a leader in digital public infrastructure. From the IRCTC’s (Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation) ticketing system and the income tax department’s e-filing to Aadhaar authentication, UPI, DigiLocker etc., India holds up proof, at home and abroad, that it can build technology that works at scale.

articles.title: MHA declares Zakir Naik’s Islamic Research Foundation unlawful for another five years
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Ministry of Home Affairs on Friday (November 13, 2026) declared Zakir Naik’s Islamic Research Foundation (IRF) an unlawful association under UAPA for another five years.
This is the third time that the ban against IRF has been extended. The outfit was first banned in 2016 .

Further, the Central Government said it believes that if the unlawful activities of the IRF were not curbed and controlled immediately, the organisation would “take the opportunity to continue its subversive activities and re-organise its activists who are still absconding; disrupt the secular fabric of the country by polluting the minds of the people by creating communal disharmony; propagate anti-national sentiments; escalate secessionism by supporting militancy and undertake activities which are prejudicial to the sovereignty, integrity and security of the country,” according to a government notification.
File picture of Mumbai Police standing guard in front of the Islamic Research Foundation's (IRF) office in 2016 | Photo Credit: Vivek Bendre

The notification further said, “In exercise of the powers by Sub-sections (1) and (3) of Section 3 of the UAPA, 1967 (37 of 1967), the Central Government hereby declares the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF) as an unlawful association and directs that this notification shall, subject to any order that may be made under Section 4 of the said Act, have effect for a period of five years from the date of its publication in the official Gazette.”
Naik, who is currently abroad, is being probed by the National Investigation Agency for alleged terror activities.

Naik was born in Mumbai, but he fled India in the wake of the July 1, 2016, bombing at a cafe in Dhaka, Bangladesh. He is accused of spreading hatred among different communities through his Peace TV and social media networks, where he has over 20 million followers.

articles.title: How did a tax proposal lead the Dutch government to the verge of collapse? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Story so far: The Dutch government came close to a collapse this week over its Tax Plan for 2027 as members of the three-party ruling coalition disagreed over an amendment to the plan. Though the plan was passed in the lowest-possible majority in the House of Representatives on Thursday (November 12, 2026) night and the government subsequently defeated a no-confidence motion, the developments have brought a rift in the coalition out in the open and threaten the future of the government led by Rob Jetten just nine-months into its 4-year term.

The Netherlands currently has a minority government by a coalition of three parties holding 66 seats in the 150-member Tweede Kamer, the lower house. The centrist D66 led by Prime Minister Jetten, the youngest premier in the country’s history, is the single largest party with 26 seats and is joined by centre-right parties People’s Party for Freedom and Democracy (VVD) and Christian Democratic Appeal (CDA), with 22 and 18 seats respectively. The government came to power in February, 117 days after a snap election in October last year necessitated by the collapse of Dick Schoof’s right-wing government as far-right leader of Freedom Party Geert Wilders withdrew his support. The months following the election that failed to produce a clear winner saw parties across political spectrum and ideologies negotiate to form a government to no effect, paving the way for the centrist parties to make do with a minority administration.

articles.title: Why RBI wants to cap select overseas remittances at ₹50 Lakh to save rupees | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The story so far: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has reportedly proposed to the Ministry of Finance tightening the limits of the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS), in an attempt likely aimed at preventing a massive outflow of dollars from India. Under the current structure, Indian residents can remit up to $250,000 (over ₹2 crore) in a financial year for purposes such as travel, education, medical treatment, and overseas investments.

The LRS is a scheme under the Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), introduced by the RBI in 2004. It covers both capital account and current account transactions. Under the capital account, transactions are permitted for opening overseas foreign currency bank accounts, purchasing property, extending interest-free loans of up to one year, and investing in foreign equity, mutual funds, and listed debt securities.

articles.title: India needs to create high-quality jobs, increase productivity growth: IMF
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment and faster creation of high-quality jobs to achieve the medium-term potential growth of 6.8%, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) said on Thursday (November 12, 2026).
In its October World Economic Outlook, the IMF had upgraded India’s medium-term potential growth to 6.8% from its earlier estimate of 6.5%.

The upgrade took into account a few factors, including favourable demographics, a large and growing domestic economy or domestic market for goods, and continued momentum on structural reforms, Julie Kozack, Communications Director, IMF, told reporters in Washington.

“But in general, like in many countries, we are encouraging India to take continuing reforms, particularly to focus on how productivity growth can be increased,” she said in response to a question from PTI .
The IMF official said that to further the medium-term potential, India would need higher productivity growth, stronger private investment, and faster creation of high-quality jobs.
Ms. Kozack said these issues will come up during the Article 4 consultations with India.

articles.title: CAG widens purview of power sector audit, starting with DISCOMs; consumer satisfaction in focus
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) is undertaking a comprehensive audit of the power sector, beginning with distribution companies (discoms), where consumer satisfaction, power trading and financial sustainability emerging as key focus areas.

The exercise will subsequently cover transmission, generation, renewable energy and the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS), with each segment’s operational and financial performance being assessed over the preceding five years, according to officials familiar with the development.

Discoms will be the first to be audited, with the ongoing phase covering their performance between FY21 and FY26. As many as 39 discoms across the country, along with five departmental undertakings, will be assessed. Privately owned discoms, however, will remain outside the scope of the exercise.
The audit commenced in July this year, with the report expected to be finalised around the middle of the next financial year. The audit of the transmission segment is scheduled to begin with FY27.
Moving beyond conventional financial and operational assessments, the CAG has directed auditors to engage directly with electricity consumers, local experts and influential groups..
“We told our auditors that it (the audit) must not be limited to a stakeholder consultation exercise, we must engage with consumers of electricity,” an official said.
The exercise will capture the experiences of around 10,000 consumers across industrial, agricultural and domestic categories, with particular emphasis on the reliability and quality of power supply.

Power trading and procurement costs will constitute another major area of scrutiny. Officials pointed out that the share of short-term power procurement in states’ overall power purchase basket has risen from around 7-8% five years ago to nearly 14% currently, with power exchanges accounting for more than 56% of such transactions.
“Ultimately, the cost at which the power is purchased would impact the end consumer of the electricity, and it also impacts financials of the entities concerned,” officials said.

The audit will also examine key operational indicators, including aggregate technical and commercial (AT&C) losses, billing and collection efficiency, alongside the financial health and long-term viability of discoms.

Discoms have been selected for the first phase given their direct interface with consumers and the cascading impact of their financial and operational performance on other segments of the power sector and the wider economy.
The CAG will also rope in the coal department to facilitate an integrated assessment of the sector.

articles.title: Retail inflation crosses RBI’s upper limit for first time in two years, comes in at 6.1% in October 2026
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Retail inflation rose to 6.1% in October 2026, crossing the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) upper threshold for the first time in two years. The continued uptick in inflation, while driven by food and fuel prices, has now spread to nearly all sectors, data released by the government on Thursday shows.

The RBI targets an inflation rate of 4% with a comfort band of 2% higher or lower than figure. Inflation as measured by the Consumer Price Index (CPI) last crossed this upper threshold of 6% in October 2024, when it came in at 6.2%. Retail inflation in October 2026 was the highest since then.

The new series of the CPI, with a base year of 2024, has sectoral data that goes back to only January 2026, which means a historical analysis is possible only up to that point. Within that, the latest data shows inflation across most categories rose to series highs in October 2026.

“Although inflation remains predominantly supply-driven, stronger consumer demand pull associated with festive-season purchases may have added to price pressures, reinforcing the RBI’s decision to raise the repo rate by 25 basis points to 5.50%,” Pranjal Ghate, economist at Brickwork Ratings said, referring to the Monetary Policy Committee’s (MPC) latest decision in early October 2026.

The data shows that inflation in the food and beverages category rose sharply to 8.5% in October 2026, the highest in the series. Coupled with this, rising fuel prices meant that inflation in the transport category also rose to 5.8% in October, a series high.

As a result of accelerating food and transport prices, inflation in the restaurant and accommodation services category jumped to 10.1% in October, the first time it has come in at double-digits in the new series.
According to Madan Sabnavis, chief economist at the Bank of Baroda, some food prices could rise further in the coming months.

“The ongoing harvest prospects will throw more light on how food prices behave,” Mr. Sabnavis said. “Area under cultivation was lower for rice, maize, oilseeds, cotton and sugarcane. It has also been reported that pulses production, especially tur, could be lower this time, which can lead to a spike in prices.”
Apart from food and fuel, the data shows that other aspects of day-to-day life have also seen prices rising at a faster pace.

Clothing and footwear, for example, saw inflation coming in at nearly 5% in October 2026 — the highest in this series — from 3.9% in the previous month. The ‘furnishings, household equipment, and routine household maintenance’ category saw inflation quicken to 3.9% in October, also a series high.
Inflation in the health category quickened to 2.05% in October 2026, the highest since January, from 1.4% in September.
The ‘housing, water, electricity, gas and other fuels’ category saw inflation of 2.9% in October, also the highest in the series.

articles.title: Two days past Deepavali, NPCI yet to announce a date for UPI MDR rollout
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Two days since Deepavali, the National Payments Council of India is yet to notify a new date for the implementation of the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions and The Hindu has learnt that “there is no announcement on this at the moment”.

When it had put the proposed additional charge on hold nearly a month ago, the NPCI had said the new date would be announced “immediately” after Deepavali. The new rate was originally supposed to have been implemented on October 15.
“There is no announcement on this at the moment,” a spokesperson at the NPCI told The Hindu when asked whether the NPCI’s date announcement was imminent.

The matter of an MDR levy on specified UPI transactions received significant pushback from merchants and petrol pump dealers alike, apart from customers who feared that merchants would pass on the extra charge on to them by way of higher prices.
The petrol pump dealers further said that the MDR charge, coupled with the fact that their dealer commission had not been revised in several years, meant that their margins would be further squeezed.

The NPCI had on October 13 announced that its UPI and Services Steering Committee had decided that “keeping in mind the festive season, Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on select Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions, shall be implemented immediately post Diwali at a date to be notified separately”.

The Hindu had at the time reported that, according to government sources, the decision to delay the implementation of MDR on UPI was made in the Prime Minister’s Office following strong appeals from traders.

Praveen Khandelwal, founder and secretary-general of the Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) and a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Lok Sabha member, had welcomed the deferment, saying that it would protect traders’ interests and sustain digital payment momentum during the festive season.

articles.title: COP31: Himalayan flash floods should push all to act ‘faster and fairer’ on climate change: UN climate chief
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: The glacial collapse and flash floods in the Himalayas this year should push everyone to act "faster and fairer" on climate change, a top United Nations official said.

Responding to a question on the issue of the Himalayas on the sidelines of the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya,Turkiye, United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) Executive Secretary Simon Stiell told PTI that transitioning away from fossil fuels in a just, orderly and equitable manner, along with tripling adaptation finance, are key to resolving the crisis.

“The glacial collapse and flash floods in the Himalayas this year are a devastating reminder of how fragile these mountain environments can be, particularly the Hindu Kush Himalayas. For years, scientists and local communities have been warning that the Himalayas are at huge risk from climate change. What is happening in the Himalayas should push us to act faster and fairer on climate change,” he said.
Proposals by Nepal and Bhutan, and separately by Kyrgyzstan, to secure formal agenda items on mountain-related issues at the 31st UN failed to secure the backing of major negotiating blocs.
COP31 leaders urge focus on climate action despite global conflicts
World leaders take stage at COP31 but big names missing

Highlighting that global heating is caused by humanity still burning huge amounts of coal, oil and gas and destroying forests, the UNFCCC Executive Secretary recalled COP28 in the UAE, where all countries agreed to transition away from fossil fuels in energy systems in a just, orderly and equitable manner.

He stated that the agreement must be delivered in full, and that it is equally essential to make faster progress on helping nations adapt to climate impacts and build their resilience, especially vulnerable nations that did practically nothing to contribute to the climate crisis.

“That means delivering in full on the tripling of adaptation finance agreed at COP30 in Brazil last year. Full delivery on all existing financial commitments by developed economies is also essential, as is boosting access to finance for those who need it most, especially those vulnerable developing nations who did the least to cause the global crisis,” Mr. Stiell told PTI .

When asked how climate-vulnerable nations can trust a platform like COP given that the agenda on tripling adaptation finance failed to be formally adopted, he said that the Fund for Responding to Loss and Damage (FRLD) has been set up to provide support to vulnerable developing countries, adding that the crisis in the Himalayas shows why the COP process is critical.

“FRLD has been in its establishment phase; it has raised and received funds. The fund is now moving into delivery with an initial provisional allocation of $21.6 million for Nepal, which is a very positive step. It's essential that FRLD continues to be capitalised and deployed to the fullest extent possible,” Mr. Stiell said, adding that FRLD alone cannot meet the scale of loss and damage.
A standalone agenda item on tripling adaptation finance was not formally adopted on the official conference agenda, as consensus could not be reached during the opening plenary on November 9.

articles.title: U.S. lawmakers summon Nvidia former CEO after affair with suspected spy

fullParagraphs: U.S. lawmakers have called Jensen Huang, an architect of the artificial intelligence boom, to face their questions in December after the Nvidia ex-CEO quit over extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy.
The scandal has wiped almost half a trillion dollars off Nvidia’s market valuation, as it raises national security fears and leaves the AI industry in uncharted waters.
“Recent reports raise serious concerns about our national security and the protection of sensitive US technology,” Republican Senator Tim Scott wrote on Thursday (November 12, 2026) on X.
Mr. Scott said he was requesting mR. Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to testify in December before the Senate Banking Committee, which he chairs.
Who is Colette Kress? Nvidia's new interim CEO following Jensen Huang’s exit
Former Nvidia CEO Huang had a relationship with a second employee, sources say
Untangling Nvidia chief Jensen Huang’s Chinese spy connection
It joins a call for a closed-door interview with the leather-jacketed, 63-year-old Huang on December 1 by three House of Representatives committees, on threat of subpoena.

Huang, who has been married to his wife Lori for over 40 years, admitted Sunday to an affair, reportedly with Alice Huang, a former senior executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. The two are not related.
U.S. intelligence reportedly circulated a memo this spring alleging she was an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Beijing has rejected the allegations.
On Wednesday, The New York Times reported a second affair, citing video of Huang being affectionate with Nvidia’s vice president of health care, Kimberly Powell.
While Nvidia’s board searches for a permanent successor to Huang, who spent 33 years at the helm of the firm he co-founded, chief Financial Officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO.

articles.title: Europe pushes for seat at Ukraine peace talks but lacks unified voice
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: European nations are seeking an envoy to represent them in talks on ending the Russia-Ukraine war, concerned that a U.S.-backed process will leave them sidelined as Moscow and Washington decide the fate of a conflict that has roiled the continent.

Whether that should be one individual or more, and who it might be, is being debated as leaders from the 27-nation European Union meet Friday (November 13, 2026) at a summit in Dublin. Senior EU officials and politicians have been suggested, but there is not yet a consensus.

What the job might entail is also unclear and contested. But there is broad agreement among governments from the U.K. to Ukraine on the need for Europe to join the ongoing negotiations involving Moscow, Kyiv and Washington.

Ukraine is eager for backup from its European allies, as it's reluctant to leave the talks solely in the hands of a U.S. administration that has often seemed to lean toward Moscow's views. Russia does not want European countries involved in direct negotiations, complaining they are financing and supplying Ukraine's military effort.
And the Europeans do not trust U.S. President Donald Trump to negotiate on their behalf after a series of tense standoffs over trade, Greenland and conflicts in Iran and Ukraine.
“Without Europeans, there is no support for Ukraine,” French President Emmanuel Macron said at the European Political Community meeting in Dublin. “There is no more U.S. support."
“At the end of the day, we will be the ones to define and decide for our future security as Europeans,” he said.

European leaders fear Russian President Vladimir Putin will press Mr. Trump to back a peace settlement that weakens not just Ukraine but broader European security. Putin has demanded that NATO troops be pulled back from Russia's borders and that no European forces be deployed in Ukraine.
British Prime Minister Andy Burnham rejected the idea that Europe was being sidelined during peace negotiations, saying “there are European voices in the room.”

“All the leaders I've spoken to today are determined to put a bit of a ring of steel around Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy as part of all of this to back him up to the hilt, and that's what we will do,” he said.
As envoys from Washington, Moscow and Kyiv met in Abu Dhabi, several European countries, including the U.K., France and Germany, attended discussions nearby.
Supporters of a single envoy, like Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni, argue that their absence has let individual countries or small groups engage in freelance diplomacy.

articles.title: As election nears, Spain's Sanchez struggles to rally disillusioned left
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: When Spain's Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called a snap election ​last month, he was betting that anger over housing and fear of the far right would rally all shades of the left behind his Socialists.
But interviews and ‌polls suggest that many potential supporters are too furious about the status quo and the perceived failings of his ​own incumbent government to oblige.

The eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal in September and her subsequent death triggered protests against a ⁠housing crisis that culminated in a general strike which unions said brought more than 3 million onto the streets on Wednesday (November 12, 2026).
"Every generation has its own struggle — for us, that struggle is housing," Mr. Sanchez said at his first rally after calling the vote.
His challenge as he prepares to face the electorate on November 29 is ‌that the protests led by movements even further to his left have moved well beyond accommodation.
"We're really tired of so many things," said Maria Torrena Perez, a 40-year-old primary school teacher at a march in ‌Madrid on Wednesday (November 11, 2026)night.

"We need decent housing. We need a quality public education system. We need a decent healthcare system. Ultimately, they're not ‌investing ⁠in what they should be investing in. And we're fed up with the policies being implemented across the board."
Two deadly ⁠train crashes, corruption convictions in Mr. Sanchez's inner circle and a rush of migrants into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta have all taken their toll on Sanchez's support.
For all his campaigning, polls show backing for his party is still hovering around the 26%-29% level recorded before he called the election.

Without a shift in the next two weeks, an alliance between the ​conservative People's Party and far-right Vox, a hardline nationalist party ‌championing tighter borders and deregulation, is seen as the most likely next government.
Interviews with left-of-centre politicians, activists and voters suggested that for many, disillusionment with the status quo outweighs the urge to keep the far right out.

The "lesser evil" pitch of a centrist government standing between them and an ever-harder right is wearing thin, echoing discontent with incumbents that has spilled into social unrest across Europe in recent months.

fullParagraphs: The story so far: Software giant Microsoft is facing a widespread outage affecting users of its Outlook email service, as well as its other workplace products. Thousands of Microsoft users in India awakened on Friday (November 13, 2026) to find their inboxes inaccessible, losing hours of productivity. According to DownDetector, over 100,000 users had initially registered complaints about Microsoft Outlook.​ Microsoft Outage: Why did Microsoft Outlook and other products go offline globally? Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors. ​
Microsoft shared on X on November 13 that a portion of infrastructure was experiencing elevated load across multiple regions, and this could likely be contributing to the connectivity errors.
Microsoft said Thursday (November 13, 2026) that it was not aware of any “malicious activity” behind the hours-long disruption of its Outlook services.
“As of now, we are not aware of any malicious activity that is causing this incident. We will continue to treat this incident with urgency and priority until full resolution,” Microsoft said.

“For a city whose economy runs on serving global clients, [the outage] is no minor inconvenience,” Sambratha Shetty, Chief Operating Officer (COO), Synergia Foundation, said. “Bengaluru’s IT firms, startups and global capability centres coordinate across time zones through email, Teams calls and shared files. When those stop, client deliveries slip, support queues pile up, and teams sit idle. For outsourcing contracts bound by strict service-level agreements, even a few hours of downtime can mean penalties and strained client trust.”

“Bengaluru’s tech leaders should treat cloud failure as certain, not hypothetical. That means backup communication channels, multi-vendor setups and regularly tested continuity plans. The city that builds resilient systems for the world must build them for itself,” the COO said.
Downdetector said that Microsoft’s outage reports on November 12 reached 74 countries and territories in about an hour, in a post on X.
“Reports about Microsoft 365, Copilot, Teams and OneDrive each rose more than a hundredfold, and Azure about a hundredfold. Xbox, GitHub and LinkedIn, also Microsoft’s, rose far less,” the post said.
“We are closely monitoring the ongoing Microsoft outage,” Air India posted on X. “Our flight operations remain unaffected.”
Cartier-owner Richemont’s first half results ⁠announcement, due ‌at ‌0600GMT, ‌has been ⁠delayed ⁠due to the global ‌disruption of Microsoft services, the ‌luxury company said ⁠on Friday.
It ‌is unclear when the ‌issue will be resolved, ⁠Richemont said.
“Due to a global Microsoft service disruption, our email support services are currently impacted, and we may not be able to receive your emails,” IndiGo airlines posted on X.

articles.title: EU leaders seek to tackle challenges at first ever AI summit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: European Union leaders gather in Dublin on Friday (November 13, 2026) for their first ​ever summit on Artificial Intelligence (AI), to debate how the bloc can catch ‌up with the United States and China and tackle ​funding issues and other problems.

The meeting comes amid mounting ⁠worries about a technology that promises to transform industries and societies but in recent months has caused alarm after a series of incidents involving rogue ‌AI agents. There was further turmoil this week with the resignation of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang , leaving the industry ‌without its biggest champion.
Leaders in Dublin will also ‌assess ⁠how to overcome other problems such as red tape and ⁠set guardrails.

“Given the rapid pace of AI development, I believe that a first dedicated discussion, at leaders’ level, is now needed on the opportunities presented by ​AI, as well as ‌on its transformative effect on our economies and societies,” European Council President Antonio Costa wrote in an invitation letter to EU leaders last week.
Mistral AI chief executive Arthur Mensch and Nobel Prize-winning ‌AI pioneer Geoffrey Hinton will brief EU leaders.

Europe will ​have to ramp up its efforts if it is to be an AI player. An initiative known ⁠as the Chips Act, implemented three years ago looks likely to fall short of its goal to attract advanced manufacturing and double the ‌bloc’s share of the global chip market to 20% by 2030.

A plan to build seven AI gigafactories to house advanced AI processors, software, cloud technology, high-speed connectivity and data centres under one roof has yet to fully take off due to the fight among EU countries over spending on competitiveness in the ‌bloc’s 2028-2034 budget.

In addition to AI, leaders are also set to discuss ​Ukraine, which has since been added as a second major topic to the agenda, a day after U.S. ⁠envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner flew into Dublin to meet Ukrainian ⁠President Volodymyr Zelenskiy following talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow.
EU leaders are likely to discuss European ‌involvement in peace negotiations and potential security guarantees the EU could offer in the event of a ceasefire, a senior EU ​official said.

articles.title: Who is Colette Kress? Nvidia's new interim CEO following Jensen Huang’s exit
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Nvidia co-founder and longtime chief executive Jensen Huang stepped down on Thursday (November 13, 2026), following reports of two extramarital affairs, one involving an Nvidia executive who reported to him and another involving a woman alleged to be a Chinese spy. While Mr. Huang apologised for being unfaithful and Nvidia investigates whether he was targeted by foreign intelligence, the chipmaker’s shares have tumbled more than 30% from their October peak.

In a bid to reclaim control, Nvidia's finance chief, Colette Kress, will assume the role of interim CEO, taking over from Mr. Huang, the company announced on Thursday (November 12, 2026). This will put her in charge of the chipmaker whose processors ​power the world’s most advanced supercomputers and AI data centers.

Ms. Kress is far from an outsider to the $4 trillion AI mammoth in the artificial intelligence industry. She joined Nvidia in September 2013 ​as executive vice president and chief financial officer and has held the post since. ​She has appeared alongside Mr. Huang on the company’s quarterly earnings calls. Prior to joining Nvidia, Ms. Kress worked at Cisco, Microsoft and Texas Instruments.
Nvidia’s ⁠revenue was $4.13 billion in the fiscal year she joined and $215.9 billion in fiscal 2026.

Before Nvidia, Ms. Kress spent nearly 25 years building her career at some of the tech sector’s biggest giants. She started out with an eight-year stint in finance roles at Texas Instruments before moving to Microsoft, where she worked from 1997 to 2010 and became CFO of the server amd Tools division.

She moved to Cisco (CSCO.O) in 2010 as senior vice president ​and chief financial officer of its Business Technology and Operations Finance organisation, where she was ​responsible for financial strategy and business development. She left for Nvidia in 2013, eventhough Nvidia was the smallest company she had ever worked for.
She holds a bachelor’s degree finance from the University of Arizona and an MBA from Southern Methodist University.

Nvidia’s stock rise over the past decade made Ms. Kress one fo the wealthiest executives in the world. Forbes ranked her No. 32 on its 2026 list of America’s richest self-made women. At the stock’s October peak, her Nvidia holdings pushed her personal net worth past $1 billion, though the recent market slide reduced her company shares to roughly $750 million. She was awarded a pay package worth $14 million for Nvidia’s fiscal 2026, according to Nvidia’s proxy statement. This also includes restricted stock units.

Executive officers at Nvidia are employed at will and have no ​individual employment, severance or change-in-control agreements, according to the company’s proxy ​statement. Nvidia ⁠has said in earlier filings that many of its peer companies offer such agreements.
In a statement on Thursday, Ms. Kress said that Nvidia’s “strength has always come from its people” and that she would build on the “extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years.”
Nvidia hasn't provided any notable new updates in its internal review. Moreover, the company didn’t address either of Mr. Huang’s relationships in its Thursday announcement.
Market watchers believe the board may still look externally for a permanent succesort t lrad the AI linchpin forward.

articles.title: What are the findings of the 2024 Hindu Kush Himalayas snow update? | Explained
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: T he Ganga river basin — India’s largest — reached a record low snow persistence in 2024, the Hindu Kush Himalaya snow update of the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD) has reported. The Brahmaputra and the Indus basins have suffered similarly, threatening water supply to millions of people. “Tragically this is yet another postcard from the frontlines of a climate crisis that is accelerating even beyond scientists’ projections and causing huge challenges in one of the most populated regions of the world,” Miriam Jackson, Cryosphere Lead at ICIMOD and a contributor to reports of the UN Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, told The Hindu .

Snow persistence is the fraction of time snow is on the ground. When this snow melts, it provides water to people and ecosystems. In the river basins of the Hindu Kush Himalaya (HKH), snowmelt is the biggest source of water in the streams. Overall, it contributes 23% of the runoff to the region’s 12 major river basins every year. The HKH mountains extend around 3,500 km over eight countries — Afghanistan, Bangladesh, Bhutan, China, India, Nepal, Myanmar, and Pakistan. These mountains are also called the “water towers of Asia” because they are the origins of 10 crucial river systems on the continent — Amu Darya, Indus, Ganga, Brahmaputra, Irrawaddy, Salween, Mekong, Yangtse, Yellow river, and Tarim. These river basins provide water to almost one-fourth of the world’s population and are a significant freshwater source for 240 million people in the HKH region.

The authors of the 2024 HKH snow update analysed data from 2003 to 2024 and found significant fluctuations in snow persistence between November and April every year, when snow accumulates above ground. Based on this, they made grim predictions of lasting impact on the people in the region as well as those downstream of the river basins.

In India, snow persistence in the Ganga, the Brahmaputra, and the Indus river basins dropped significantly in 2024. The Ganga river basin noted its lowest snow persistence in 22 years, 17% below the long-term historical average (also known as ‘normal’). The previous holder of this dubious distinction was 2018, when it was 15.2% below normal. In 2015, on the other hand, snow persistence was 25.6% above normal.

Similarly, snow persistence in the Brahmaputra basin was 14.6% below normal in 2024. It was worse in 2021, when the average persistence was 15.5% below normal. In the Indus river basin, snow persistence fell 23.3% below normal this year although this was offset by excesses in parts of the lower altitudes.

Outside India, the basin of the Amu Darya river — which flows through Central Asia — recorded its lowest snow persistence in 2024: 28.2% below normal. The figure for the Helmand river, an important source of drinking water for Iran and Afghanistan, was almost 32% below normal in 2024, beating a record set in 2018. Persistence in the part where the Mekong river originates in the Himalaya was only slightly below normal this time. (This river’s delta is Vietnam’s “rice bowl”.)
The primary reason for the lower persistence in 2024 was weak western disturbances, ICIMOD remote sensing specialist and author of the report Sher Muhammad told The Hindu .

“Due to changing climate and global warming, this pattern is becoming increasingly unstable. Although the exact mechanisms are not fully understood, global warming is thought to exacerbate prolonged and intense La Niña–El Niño conditions. These phases of a recurring climate pattern across the tropical Pacific Ocean significantly influence global weather patterns, including western disturbances,” he added.

Western disturbances are low-pressure systems that originate over the Mediterranean Sea, the Caspian, and the Black Seas and bring rain and snow to the HKH region in winter. “The region where these storms originate experienced persistently high sea-surface temperatures,” Mr. Muhammad explained. “This disruption weakened and delayed the arrival of the western disturbance, resulting in reduced winter precipitation and snowfall in the HKH region. The pattern of high temperatures and altered weather systems explains both the record low snow persistence in 2024 and similar historical records.”

“We have warned for years that the 1.5 degrees Celsius limit that governments signed up to in the Paris Agreement is not ambitious enough to protect the snow and ice, people and nature of the Hindu Kush Himalayas because the target is a global average, and the real temperature increase will be far higher here,” Ms. Jackson added.

The persistence of snow in China’s Yellow River basin exceeded the normal value by 20.2% in 2024. “The Yellow river basin is an area where the East Asian winter monsoon brings cold, dry air from Siberia and Mongolia,” Mr. Muhammad said. “When this cold air mass interacts with moist air from other regions, particularly the Pacific Ocean, it can result in snowfall over the higher altitudes of the upper Yellow River basin.”

“When the cold air from the east Asian winter monsoon systems interacts with moist air masses from the Pacific Ocean, it can result in snowfall at higher elevations in the eastern Himalaya,” Mr. Muhammad added.

articles.title: Jewellery and souvenir made from plastic discarded in the Himalayas
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Have you ever wondered what happens to discarded plastic bottle caps? At best, they transform into wheels in DIY toy projects; or so we think. In Nepal, they are recycled into souvenirs, jewellery and everyday utility items by Nepal-based Moware. This design intervention enterprise Eva Villardon Grande gives a new meaning to waste left behind in the Himalayas.

Launched in 2013, Moware which stands for ‘Mountain Waste Repurpose’, employs innovative ways to reduce our footprint by upcycling and creatively transforming waste into useful products. The initiative was kickstarted to promote paper waste management in offices, even as it generated employment for low-income women from Lalitpur, Kathmandu. Over the years, they diversified, experimenting extensively with waste aluminium, wrappers, and glass bottles.
The Himalayan stones - Renjo La, Cho La and Kongma La | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Among their collectables, the most talked about is the From the Himalayas collection including a miniature model of the mountains that shows its most iconic peaks — Shartse, Lhotse, Mount Everest, Nuptse, Changtise Peak, Khumbutse Peak, and Mount Lingtren. The collection also includes ornamental rocks, jewellery and candle stand, all made from plastic bottle caps discarded by trekkers in the Himalayas.
Plastic bottle caps at Moware’s workshop | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

The glass in the collection are made from recycled alcohol bottles that are left behind by tourists. These are collected from hotels by Waste management companies. Moware sources these and turns them into utility items. An average trekker uses approximately 38 water bottles during the climb. Moware decided to see what could be done with the plastic instead of sending it to landfills, or having it incinerated. Towards this end, they set out to collaborate with two like-minded waste product resource management companies, Blue Waste and Sagarmatha Next., based out of Nepal, to find a solution.

Carry Me Back was the first initiative of Sagarmatha Next to address the waste management challenge in the Sagarmatha National Park and the Khumbu region (Nepalese side of Mount Everest). When the pilot project of the crowdsourced waste removal system was initiated in 2019, 2,500 tourists transported about 4,000 kilograms of waste. The waste is segregated, packed in specially made bags and left at a pick-up station located by the stupa in Namche Bazaar.
Eva and her team members at Moware | Photo Credit: Special arrangement

Why bottle caps? Eva explains, “While a plastic bottle without the cap may have a lot of takers, the plastic cap itself — made from High-Density Polyethylene (HDP) — finds no takers, so they eventually end up in landfills.”

Moware then collaborated with Pim and Luc of Super Local, a team of Dutch designers based in Nepal. The duo devoted themselves to reducing waste and creating sustainable products hand-in-hand with local communities. “After a few months of brainstorming, they devised the Himalayan model design and Himalayan stones. The Himalayan stone are assortment of three mani stones — Renjo La, Cho La and Kongma La. These stones represent the awe-inspiring three passes of the Khumbu region. We just loved it and saw a beautiful chance to give the caps a new life,” says Eva who has made Nepal her home for now, to work on similar projects.

Why Himalayan stones? Eva continued, “We discovered trekkers and hikers pick stones as reminder of the trip when they visit the Everest. Many do not know that this is forbidden. This is how we decided on assortment of three mani stones — Renjo La, Cho La and Kongma La. They are made of 8, 10 and 16 bottle caps respectively.”

“With the help from our sister concern Sagarmatha Next (the first project of Himalayan Museum and Sustainability Park) we have collected and transformed 60,000 kilograms of waste generated in Kathmandu Valley and the Khumbu region,” she explains, adding that about 5,40,000 tonnes of solid waste are generated every year in Nepal. “Despite the efforts made to improve waste management practices, the country lacks a formal system for reusing and recycling. Consequently, many valuable resources are thrown away without recovery and treatment,” says Eva.

articles.title: In a dilemma: On Sheikh Hasina and India-Bangladesh ties
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Bangladesh’s former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina now in exile in India, has set off speculation about her imminent return to Dhaka by submitting an application for a new Bangladeshi passport and national identity card this week. The application, made through the Bangladesh High Commission in Delhi, was dismissed by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s Foreign Affairs Adviser Humayun Kabir, who said that the government in Dhaka would not grant a passport to a “terrorist”, and would seek her return via the extradition agreement as a “prisoner transfer process” with India. Ms. Hasina has already announced that she plans to return to Bangladesh in December this year, as she did after her previous stay in India in exile from 1975-1981, after the brutal assassination of her father Sheikh Mujibur Rahman and nearly every other member of her family. However, the situation is considerably different now. This time, Ms. Hasina came to India in 2024 fleeing mobs of protestors that overthrew her government, and has since been convicted by a tribunal for ordering a crackdown on thousands of students, and sentenced to death. In interviews, including to The Hindu , Ms. Hasina says she hopes to return to Bangladesh to argue her case and rebuild her party, the Awami League, but that is hardly likely, given the anger against her amongst the polity, and bipartisan consensus to ban the Awami League from politics. Despite the harsh rhetoric it employs against her, the BNP government is unlikely to wish for her return, as it would have to begin execution proceedings against the 79-year-old former Prime Minister, with international opposition to such a move expected to be voluble. Not doing so would only strengthen its opposition party, the Jamaat-e-Islami, that has accused the Rahman government of soft-pedalling the issue. The government must also worry about possible protests and violence within the country in the event Ms. Hasina returns.

The situation puts the Modi government in a spot. Ever since Ms. Hasina announced plans to return, during a virtual press conference held in Delhi on August 5 this year, Delhi-Dhaka ties have been on a downslide. The government’s decision not to prevent Ms. Hasina from addressing the press, where she used the opportunity to soundly criticise PM Rahman, meant the abrupt cancellation of the Bangladesh PM’s visit. Next month, the Indo-Bangladesh Ganga Water treaty is set to expire, and talks on its extension have also become a casualty. Ms. Hasina has been an honoured guest in India, and the government cannot physically restrain her from taking the flight to Dhaka or travelling to the land border at Petrapole to cross over. Nor can it wash its hands of her situation once she crosses over. New Delhi must redouble its diplomatic efforts on improving bilateral ties while also ensuring Ms. Hasina’s welfare.

articles.title: New deal: On COP31 and lofty climate goals
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The 31st Conference of Parties (COP) began this week in Antalya, Türkiye. Hosted by Türkiye and negotiations presided over by Australia, the run-up to the gathering saw ministerial delegations visit Fiji and Tuvalu. This was to serve as a stark reminder of the purpose of COPs, namely that it was small island nations that are most vulnerable to warming from rising greenhouse gas emissions. However, the opening days have belied this sense of urgency. Prominent world leaders, even from the European countries who as a group champion the cause most vociferously, have chosen to skip the meet. The agenda and pre-summit expectations suggest that the main concerns this year are likely to be about delivering on existing commitments such as delivering $300 billion a year by 2035, which was decided at COP29 in Baku, as well as the COP30 call to triple the adaptation finance during that interval. However, deciding how these climate funds will practically flow has been deferred to COP32. The second global stocktake, a periodic check on progress under the Paris Agreement, begins at COP31, but the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) has dithered on a timeline for the next reports that will serve as the scientific push to policy makers to accelerate efforts towards keeping a rise in temperatures below 2°C, and more ambitiously 1.5°C.

The previous edition of COP30 concluded without a formal roadmap away from fossil fuels — a step back from the COP28 consensus in Dubai. There is a voluntary roadmap ahead of COP31 but it is out of the formal negotiating text. In the background of the West Asia war, the withdrawal of the United States from the Paris Agreement and financial strain writ large over Europe, funds are a challenge as evidenced in the recent Loss and Damage fund approval to Nepal of $21 million when the ask is in billions. COP31 president, Murat Kurum has laid an electrification target, which is to raise electricity’s share from 23% of total energy consumption to 35% by 2035. India has already refused to sign such a pledge and insisted on predictable climate finance, technology transfer, and nationally determined approaches to climate mitigation. These negotiations have a character of their own and deliberating nations must strive to get nations to deliver on past promises rather than commit to new lofty targets.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: Without any rationale: On the disbanding of the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations.

articles.title: Modi in Bengaluru: PM flags off elevated stretch of Namma Metro Pink Line | LIVE
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The opening of the elevated section of the Pink Line is expected to offer only minor relief to the city’s gridlock, with the crucial underground section connecting the Central Business District to north Bengaluru awaiting completion, writes Darshan Devaiah B.P. Mind the gap: Partial opening of Namma Metro Pink Line leaves commuters wanting Partial opening of Bengaluru's Namma Metro Pink Line offers limited relief; underground North-South link remains pending until 2027.
Partial opening of Bengaluru's Namma Metro Pink Line offers limited relief; underground North-South link remains pending until 2027.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi flagged off the elevated section of Bengaluru’s Pink Line Metro at S.G. Palya (Suddagunte Palya) Metro Station, in the presence of Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav and Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar.

The Pink Line is part of Namma Metro’s Phase II and is designed to connect Kalena Agrahara in south Bengaluru with Nagawara in north Bengaluru. The 21.25-km corridor comprises a 7.5-km elevated section and a 13.76-km underground section.
Once fully operational, the corridor is projected to carry approximately 3.76 lakh passengers daily, according to the Detailed Project Report (DPR).

Mr. Modi later travelled by Metro to Bilekahalli-IIMB Metro Station accompanied by Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav, Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda and Bengaluru South MP Tejasvi Surya.
Before entering the platform, Mr Modi purchased a Metro ticket. BMRCL officials briefed him on the project before he boarded the train, a BMRCL source told The Hindu .

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Karnataka Governor Sudha Yadav have arrived by helicopter at the R.A. Mundkur Fire and Emergency Services Training Centre campus near Dairy Circle on Bannerghatta Road in Bengaluru.

Modi will proceed to S.G. Palya (Suddagunte Palya) Metro Station, where he, along with Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar, will flag off the Pink Line Metro service and undertake a ride to Bilekahalli-IIMB Metro Station.

The PM will also unveil plaques marking the foundation stone-laying of three projects, including a compressed biogas plant at Haralakunte village in Bengaluru South and two power transmission projects.
He will also inaugurate renewable energy transmission schemes in Koppal, Gadag and Bidar.
The programme also includes dedication of an 80 TMT LPG cavern developed by HPCL, the Devangonthi Marketing Terminal of MRPL, railway doubling and electrification projects.

articles.title: Central Railway to run four special Mumbai-Nagpur trains between November 13-15
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Central Railway has announced four special train services between Mumbai and Nagpur from November 13 to 15 to accommodate additional passenger traffic during the festive season.

According to a press release issued on Thursday (November 12, 2026), two services will operate between Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus (CSMT) and Nagpur, while two others will run between Lokmanya Tilak Terminus (LTT) and Nagpur.

Train No. 01125 will depart from CSMT at 3.25 p.m. on November 13 and reach Nagpur at 7 a.m. the following day. On its return journey, Train No. 01126 will leave Nagpur at 4.10 p.m. on November 14 and arrive at CSMT at 8.05 a.m. the next day.
The CSMT-Nagpur special will halt at Dadar, Thane, Kalyan, Igatpuri, Nashik Road, Chalisgaon, Jalgaon, Bhusaval, Malkapur, Shegaon, Akola, Badnera, Dhamangaon and Wardha.

Similarly, Train No. 01129 will depart from LTT at 3.25 p.m. on November 14 and reach Nagpur at 7 a.m. the following day. The return service, Train No. 01130, will leave Nagpur at 4.10 p.m. on November 15 and arrive at LTT at 8.05 a.m. the next day.
The LTT-Nagpur special will stop at the same stations as the CSMT service, except Dadar.
Both special trains will have AC, sleeper and general-class coaches.
The CSMT-Nagpur service will also include AC three-tier economy coaches.

Central Railway said bookings for the reserved coaches are open at computerised reservation centres and through the IRCTC website. Tickets for unreserved coaches can be booked through the UTS system or the RailOne app at normal charges.
Passengers can check detailed schedules and stoppage timings through the National Train Enquiry System website or mobile application.

articles.title: Gig and platform workers’ strike call in Hyderabad on November 14, plan major rally

fullParagraphs: Gig and platform workers have called for a strike in the city on November 14 to demand social security, workers’ rights, and welfare measures, according to the Telangana Gig and Platform Workers’ Union (TGPWU).

TGPWU office-bearer Shaik Salauddin said on Thursday that Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has been invited to join the rally with the union extending gratitude to him for “his advocacy and action for the welfare of gig and platform workers”, especially against the backdrop of the 2023 Bharat Jodo Yatra.

“The Telangana Gig and Platform Workers Act 2026 provides a vital legal framework for worker rights, centered on mandatory registration, social security benefits, a dedicated welfare board, and an effective grievance redressal mechanism. The state government has formulated the rules for implementing the Act, initiating steps to constitute the Welfare Board and launching a dedicated app to register workers and resolve grievances ,” Mr. Salauddin said.

articles.title: The SIR exercise is also a technology failure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Much of the public argument over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of India’s electoral rolls is around law, power and politics. The autonomy of the Election Commission of India (ECI), the list of acceptable documents, and the burden placed on voters to prove eligibility are the key focus issues. There is, of course, no doubt that these questions matter. But a quieter, less spoken-about story runs underneath them. The 2025-26 SIR is the first revision of this scale to be run through a centralised digital platform, and the technology itself has become a source of exclusion. Viewed as a nationwide digital transformation project, the SIR fails on several counts that any student of technology would immediately recognise.

The irony stares right at us. India presents itself, with ample reasons to do so, as a leader in digital public infrastructure. From the IRCTC’s (Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation) ticketing system and the income tax department’s e-filing to Aadhaar authentication, UPI, DigiLocker etc., India holds up proof, at home and abroad, that it can build technology that works at scale.
