articles.title: Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Several industry bodies have recommended to the Ministry of Finance that the upcoming Budget 2027 should rationalise the Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on equities and reduce the rate of the Securities Transaction Tax (STT).

Officials in the Finance Ministry, including Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava, have been conducting their pre-Budget consultative meetings, during which they met the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI), and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM), among others.

One of the most-cited requests from the industry was the rationalisation of LTCG on equities. In Budget 2026, the Centre removed the 12.5% LTCG tax in the government securities market for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) alongside other measures including reforms under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR).

Currently, foreign and domestic investors have to pay 12.5% tax on the sale of equities on gains exceeding Rs 1.25 lakh per annum on listed shares. The Centre has held several meetings with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and other industry players.

“Removing the LTCG levy would raise post-tax returns and close a gap with Korea, Taiwan and Brazil,” Rakesh Nangia, chairman of task force on International Taxes at ASSOCHAM said. “The debt market is a useful precedent, which after the G-sec relief, saw FPI inflows rise to about $9 billion in June-July.”

The PHDCCI has requested that the government abolish LTCG tax on equity investments, reduce the short-term capital gains (STCG) tax rate from 20% to 10%, and lower STT rates “to encourage long-term investment and improve India’s capital market competitiveness”.

In its representation to Ms. Sitharaman, FICCI highlighted the fact that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn about Rs 3.08 lakh crore during the year. It added that capital gains tax, which is charged over and above the STT, erodes returns from equities, and needs a review to make India a more attractive place to invest.

However, other market players highlight that the revenue loss incurred from the removal of LTCG could be negated through a hike in STT. According to estimates by SBI Research, the removal of LTCG would result in a revenue loss of Rs 40,000-50,000 crore for FY28.

One of the key frictions for FPIs underscored by industry bodies and equity analysts is the computation of the tax. Under Income-Tax Act, the calculation of the LTCG is in the Indian rupee. The challenge arises due to currency depreciation as against the investor’s base currency during the holding period, due to which investors are still liable to pay tax even when net returns in dollar terms are flat or even negative. This issue is currently under examination.

VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Financial Services also cautioned against selective relief, noting that abolishing LTCG solely for FPIs would be discriminatory against domestic retail and direct equity investors who remain subject to the 12.5% tax. He urged any tax relief must apply equally across the board to ensure a level playing field.

Industry experts also suggest that while amendments in tax laws are just one part of attracting inflows, what remains important is continued momentum in corporate earnings growth, policy certainty and a stable rupee.

As such, simplifying onboarding and setting one predictable tax clearance process at exit coupled with making dispute resolution faster and binding is what would bring stable long-term investments, Nangia noted.

articles.title: Amidst simmering tensions, India-Bangladesh consular dialogue postponed
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Days after Bangladesh’s deposed Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina requested Dhaka for a new passport and national identity card, the fifth India-Bangladesh consular dialogue that was scheduled to take place on November 17 and 18 has been postponed, a diplomatic source has confirmed.

The source indicated that the postponement of the dialogue was mainly on account of growing tensions in the bilateral relationship caused by Ms. Hasina’s announcement that she will return to Bangladesh next month.

The planned consular dialogue would have been the first such meeting between the two sides in more than two years. The last such dialogue was held in New Delhi on May 29, 2024, just over two months before the Hasina government fell in a youth-led uprising in Dhaka.

The consular dialogue was scheduled to be held in Dhaka at the level of Director Generals of the Foreign Ministries of both countries. The planned agenda included issues of border management, visa procedures, and the repatriation of citizens detained on both sides. The number of Indian visas issued was drastically reduced when tensions broke out in August 2024. According to sources, India has gradually increased the number of visas issued to travellers from Bangladesh in recent months, especially after the election of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in February this year.

The two countries started a consular dialogue in 2017 to “strengthen people-to-people contacts by having a regular channel of communication on consular, visa, and mutual legal assistance cooperation matters between India and Bangladesh.” Four rounds of consular dialogues were held during the rule of the Awami League in Dhaka. As per the Ministry of External Affairs, the fourth round held in May 2024 discussed issues like “visa matters, repatriation, Mutual Legal Assistance Treaty cases etc.”

Attempts at normalising the India-Bangladesh relationship in recent months have been hindered by Ms. Hasina’s presence in India, where she took refuge on August 5, 2024. On November 9 this year, a London-based legal firm representing Ms. Hasina wrote to the High Commission of Bangladesh in New Delhi requesting a new passport and the national ID card. “In view of the reported revocation of her existing Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card (NID) by the Interim Government and other authorities, I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client,” said the letter sent by the law firm Matrix Chambers.

However, the Acting Foreign Minister of Bangladesh Humayun Kabir responded to this development by telling journalists that Bangladesh would not issue a passport to Ms. Hasina. Instead, he said, Dhaka would seek Ms. Hasina’s extradition under an “acceptable prisoner exchange process”, adding that such a handover would have to be conducted carefully and under proper surveillance.

articles.title: Centre sanctions new roads, infrastructure along China’s border
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Amid continuing face-offs with the Chinese Army along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) in Arunachal Pradesh since late July, the Indo-Tibetan Border Police (ITBP) has sanctioned the construction of new border infrastructure in the northeastern State, a senior government official told The Hindu .

Earlier, in February, the Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS) had cleared the third phase of the Indo-China Border Roads (ICBR-III) project. Under the scheme, as many as 26 roads are to be constructed along the LAC in Arunachal Pradesh, another government official said. The Union Government has not yet officially announced the ICBR-III project or publicly disclosed these details.
This is only the second time after the 2020 Galwan clashes in eastern Ladakh that a critical road infrastructure project has been sanctioned along the border with China.

The first phase of the ICBR was initiated in 2005 when it was decided that the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) would construct 27 priority roads with a total length of 608 km along the border with China.

The second phase of the ICBR, comprising 32 roads with a total length of 683 km, was approved on September 21, 2020, just months after 20 Indian soldiers were killed in violent clashes with the Chinese People’s Liberation Army in eastern Ladakh.

Since September, the ITBP has authorised the construction of 15 pedestrian suspension bridges and 18 log bridges in Upper Subansiri and Kurung Kumey districts, covering the areas bordering China in Arunachal Pradesh.

The project clearance came days after India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit from September 11 to 13 in New Delhi, which was attended by Chinese President Xi Jinping. A government statement after the meeting said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasised that peace and tranquillity in the border areas remains an essential basis for the continued development of bilateral relations. He underlined the need for both sides to observe existing agreements and understandings on border-related issues.

In December 2020, the MHA had approved construction of 18 pedestrian tracks, including foot suspension bridges, log bridges, and staging camps, measuring a total length of 598.27 km in the border areas of Arunachal Pradesh.
On October 22 this year, former ITBP Director-General Shatrujeet Kapur mentioned that the “face-off” with Chinese troops “continues at several locations in Arunachal Pradesh.”

Addressing the Himveer Samman Samaroah at the Central Training College at Alwar in Rajasthan, Mr. Kapur said: “In the past few days, a situation arose where face-offs happened at several locations in Arunachal and it still continues. Our Shaurya commandos played an exemplary role in this.”

The 1-hour 13-minute long video recording of Mr. Kapur’s speech — in which he also stressed the need to invest and develop drone and counter-drone technology, noting that it may not be possible to face China through traditional methods as they have invested a lot in the modernisation of their weapons and infrastructure — has since been taken down from the ITBP’s official YouTube page.

The tension in Arunachal Pradesh has persisted even though India and China have held three high-level border talks since July. On August 6, the 36th WMCC (Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs) meeting was held. This was followed by the 25th round of talks between the Special Representatives on the boundary question on August 26 in Beijing, where India was represented by National Security Advisor Ajit Doval. On September 6, the first-ever Corps Commander-level meetings between the two armies were held in the Eastern Sector at the Vacha-Damai border personnel meeting point in Arunachal Pradesh Such meetings have so far largely been held at the Chushul-Moldo border meeting point in eastern Ladakh, particularly after the Galwan Valley clashes of June 2020.

fullParagraphs: Jensen Huang resigned as chief executive of Nvidia on Thursday (November 12, 2026), ending his 33-year run at the helm of the AI giant he co-founded after revelations he had two extramarital affairs, including with a woman accused of spying for China .

The company’s board said Mr. Huang had stepped down as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim CEO while keeping her finance role, and the board will consider internal and external candidates for a permanent replacement.

Mr. Huang faced growing calls to resign after his affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Late Wednesday (November 11, 2026), media reports said Mr. Huang had another extramarital affair with an Nvidia employee who reports to him.

articles.title: U.S. envoys meet Putin at Kremlin following Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: U.S. President Donald Trump's envoys arrived at the Kremlin on Thursday (November 12, 2026) for talks with President Vladimir Putin, as Washington sought to generate new momentum in peace efforts after two days of U.S.-mediated negotiations between the Russian and Ukrainian delegations.

Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, who is also Mr.Trump's son-in-law, brokered the talks in Abu Dhabi, the capital of the United Arab Emirates, which were the first direct discussions between Russian and Ukrainian officials in nine months as the push for peace stalled this year.
The talks wrapped up on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) with an agreement on a large exchange of prisoners, with the exact number still to be agreed.

The talks produced no visible breakthrough in ending the nearly five years of large-scale hostilities, which began on February 24, 2022, after the fighting initially started in 2014 in eastern Ukraine.
But Mr. Kushner and Mr. Witkoff appeared keen to seize the moment and went straight to the Kremlin.

Mr. Kushner said that one of the goals of the meeting with Mr. Putin is to get the Russian leader's blessing for European representatives to be part of the talks, which are looking at the continent's broader security arrangements.
The U.S. and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy are looking for Europe to appoint a single person to negotiate with Moscow.

At the moment, Moscow doesn't want European countries, which are concerned about Russia's conduct and broader intentions on the continent, involved in the direct negotiations. Moscow complains that Europe is financing and supplying weaponry to Ukraine and is part of the problem holding up a deal.

Many in Europe see the inclusion of Russia in discussions about European security as an unwelcome concession to Mr. Putin, who has described NATO's eastward expansion as a top security threat to his country. Moscow has demanded that the trans-Atlantic alliance's troops be pulled back from Russia's borders.
Some analysts say negotiators may be looking to grant Russia concessions on NATO's strategy in return for peace in Ukraine — a possibility that has alarmed European governments.

After meeting with Mr. Putin, Mr. Kushner said that he and Mr. Witkoff will fly to Dublin, Ireland, to meet later on Thursday (November 12, 2026) with Mr. Zelenskyy, who is attending a meeting of more than 40 European countries that also includes NATO Secretary-General Mark Rutte.

Mr. Zelenskyy said that political changes, including Democrats taking over the U.S. Congress in January following the U.S. midterm elections and votes in France next year, could bring “a window of opportunity” for a peace deal.

articles.title: Modi to visit Manila for ASEAN Summit; maritime security, trade on agenda
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will travel to Manila on Monday (November 16, 2026) for a three-day visit to attend the annual India-ASEAN summit that is expected to focus on boosting maritime security cooperation and enhancing trade and investment ties.
He will also attend the annual East Asia Summit. Philippines is hosting the summits in its capacity as the current chair of the 11-nation ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations).

Mr. Modi is also set to join Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese, U.S. President Donald Trump, and Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi for the annual Quad summit in Manila. There is, however, no official word on the Quad summit.
At the India-ASEAN and the East Asia summits, New Delhi is expected to pitch for deeper maritime cooperation among the like-minded nations in the Indo-Pacific.
The ASEAN is considered one of the most influential groupings in the region, and India and several other countries including the U.S., China, Japan and Australia are its dialogue partners.

"Prime Minister Modi will be travelling to Manila to attend the 23rd ASEAN-India summit and the 21st meeting of the ASEAN-led East Asia Summit process. The visit will take place from November 16 to 18," said Rudrendra Tandon, Secretary (East) in the External Affairs Ministry.

He said Mr. Modi's programme in Manila will include attending a dinner to be hosted by the President of the Philippines Ferdinand Marcos Jr. for the visiting dignitaries of this summit process and bilateral meetings.
Mr. Modi will attend the ASEAN-India Summit and the East Asia Summit process on November 17.
The top official said enhancing maritime security and trade and investment ties will be among the key focus areas at the Summit.

The East Asia Summit is the premier forum in the Asia-Pacific region to deal with issues relating to security and defence. Since its inception in 2005, it has played a significant role in the strategic, geopolitical, and economic evolution of East Asia.
Apart from the ASEAN member states, the East Asia Summit includes India, China, Japan, the Republic of Korea, Australia, New Zealand, the U.S. and Russia.
"There is also a very strong demand from the Indian community to meet the Prime Minister. So we are trying to adjust that also in his schedule," Mr. Tandon said at a media briefing.

articles.title: New York building collapse: At least 8 people dead as rescuers dig through rubble
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: At least eight people have died after a three-story building in Brooklyn collapsed at the edge of a construction site, New York City’s Mayor said on Thursday (November 12, 2026), as firefighters kept digging through the rubble to find others who may be trapped beneath the wreckage.
The building came down on Wednesday afternoon (November 11, 2026). At least 17 people have been injured, including three firefighters, Mayor Zohran Mamdani said.

articles.title: India undergoing massive transformation in renewable energy: Earthshot Prize CEO
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: India is at the forefront of climate solutions, and its innovations have immediate global application, especially when it comes to issues such as heat stress, Earthshot Prize CEO Jason Knauf said. He was speaking with The Hindu on Thursday (November 12, 2026) on the background of the launch of the five-day Earthshot Prize summit, which will take place in Mumbai and Jaipur from November 13 to 17.

As COP31 gathers in Türkiye for climate negotiations, it is India and Mumbai which will send a message of climate solutions, he said. “There is a race going on right now. The first country that can have access to cheap, clean and abundant energy, is going to have a huge economic advantage. And I think, India knows that. Which is why so much is being done here to use the huge solar resource that India has,” he said.

Earthshot Prize is one of the world’s most prestigious environmental awards. It was founded by Prince William six years ago. This is the first time the awards are being held in India. Prince William will be in India for the events.

On Thursday (November 12, 2026), Mr. Knauf spoke about how India was an inspiration behind starting the award, why the awards are being held in India and particularly in Mumbai this year, and the lessons he has learnt during his stay in the country. Observing that India is undergoing a “massive transformation” about renewable energy, he said it had an advantage over other countries to bring in sustainable climate solutions. He said there was no debate between economic progress and environmental protection anymore. “What is good for the environment is good for business, and Indian companies are showing that,” Mr. Knauf said, adding that the past Indian winners had been able to raise $800 million in commercial international investment after winning the Earthshot Prize.
The Earthshot Prize is slated to make large announcements about two Indian finalists — Mahindra Last Mile Mobility and Mahila Housing Trust, in the coming week.

Mr. Knauf said climate action conversation needed to move beyond the ‘environment bubble’. Acknowledging India’s efforts in the conservation sector, he said it was important to showcase India’s optimism to the world. Adding that the inspiration behind the awards came from India too, he spoke of how the Prince of Wales saw environmental action during his visit to India in 2016, when he was inspired by the country’s approach towards working with nature.

“For a country that is on the frontline of the environmental issues despite having not caused them, people are more optimistic about their abilities to solve them, than many richer countries. That tells you something. We all have to learn from that example. We are happy that the Earthshot Prize is coming here to celebrate that Indian spirit for the whole world,” Mr. Knauf said. He added that Mumbai was chosen as it was the financial and entertainment capital of the country.

“Earthshot Prize is about getting out to people. We want to get out to investors, to corporate leaders. We also want to tap into the world of entertainment and sporting. Mumbai is the perfect place for that. It is the global capital for the financial sector and the entertainment world,” he said.

This year, Earthshot Prize ceremony will be held at an unprecedented scale, he said, adding that over 5,000 people would participate in the events which would draw people from different countries, and children from over 24 States of India. The event would be live telecast around 240 countries for the first time.

Asked about how he saw the climate challenge, Mr. Knauf said he was an eternal optimist. “At Earthshot, we have a simple equation — urgency + optimism = action. Anyone who wants to give up and be negative, that is a big threat to action. As big a threat as carbon emissions. Because the second we decide that the issues are too hard, then we look the other way. That is giving up, and particularly for the next generation that is coming, it is an unacceptable attitude,” he said.

articles.title: ISRO successfully carries out ground static test of PSLV third stage
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) which is looking to get its workhorse launcher, the Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV), back on track has successfully carried out the ground static test of the PSLV third stage (PS3) at the Static Test Facility in Satish Dhawan Space Centre, Sriharikota on Thursday (November 12, 2026).

“Subsequent to the anomalies observed in the third stage of PSLV during the PSLV-C61/EOS-09 & PSLV-C62 / EOS-N1 missions, the configuration of the PS3 stage was revisited comprehensively with respect to the design margins, raw material acceptance criteria, assembly procedures, and the quality checks that were followed so far,” ISRO said.

“The configuration has been strengthened and essential improvements have been carried out in the nozzle configuration to improve design margins along with updated procedures in the acceptance of raw materials, assembly procedures and quality checks,” ISRO added.
It also said that the mechanical interfaces have been strengthened with redundancy in the sealing systems and adequacy of the design margins have been verified.

“The updates in assembly procedures and non-destructive tests (NDT) during the various phases of integration and transportation have been implemented and the new version of the PS3 solid motor stage is realised and tested successfully,” ISRO said.
Based on the detailed analysis and reviews of the test data, the space agency said further tests are planned.

articles.title: Study suggests not all obesity means ill-health
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Only between a quarter and a third of people currently diagnosed with obesity should be considered as in poor health, according to a new study that joins calls to overhaul how the condition is diagnosed.

The study, published in Nature on Wednesday, follows a proposal last year from experts and medical organisations to move obesity diagnosis beyond just body mass index (BMI), based on a person’s weight and height, to include body fat and broader health.

The study attempts to show what this new definition could mean for diagnosis levels, prevalence, and ultimately, treatment, for a condition the World Health Organization currently estimates affects more than one billion people globally.

Obesity can be a risk factor for type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, liver and kidney disease and cancer. The study suggests defining it as pre-clinical, when the condition is largely a risk factor, and clinical, when it is causing ill health.

Using data from almost 850,000 adults from China, Britain, the US and Spain, the study estimates that under the new framework, 1% to 3% of those defined as obese using BMI alone would not be, while another 5% to 9%, with higher body fat for example, would be diagnosed with the condition. Across a population, this could affect tens of millions of people.
The study’s senior author Francesco Rubino, professor and chair of metabolic and bariatric surgery at King’s College London, said the inaccuracy of BMI measurements was well-known.

“But we haven’t so far got a better system,” he said. That is what the new framework aims to do, he added, saying it could “provide a meaningful clinical characterisation of obesity that can inform care and policy.”

The new framework proposes measuring body fat, including by waist circumference, as well as BMI, and considering if a patient has any organ dysfunction linked to weight, like heart or liver problems, before making a diagnosis.

This means some people with high BMI alone would not be classed as having obesity. Those who have high body fat and high BMI would be diagnosed with “pre-clinical obesity”, and those who also have organ dysfunction would have “clinical obesity” – considered an active disease that would usually require more urgent treatment.
Under these criteria, only on average roughly 27% of people with obesity across the four studied countries have clinical obesity, the study estimated – representing around 8.5% of all adults.

The majority of those with “pre-clinical obesity” – around 82% on average across the four countries studied – did not progress to clinical obesity, although progression rates were higher in China and Spain, the study found.

articles.title: CAR-T trial deaths do not deter lupus patients hoping for a cure
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Prelims: ISRO/NASA Missions, Defense Updates, Tech & Climate Reports
fullParagraphs: Lupus patients struggling with the debilitating disease are lining up to try experimental CAR-T therapies even after the recent deaths of four patients in clinical trials for a variety of autoimmune diseases, according to doctors who treat the life-threatening condition.
The trials remain halted and full details of the deaths — three linked to Novartis and one to Bristol Myers Squibb — have not been released.
Still, patients are willing to take the risk, compelled by accounts of people with advanced disease who were able to stop all medications and reclaim normal lives.

“I have patients that are literally waiting to get in,” said Dr. Anca Askanase, chief of rheumatology at the Hospital for Special Surgery in New York, who has enrolled patients in the Bristol Myers CAR-T trials.

Systemic lupus erythematosus, or SLE, the most common and severe form of lupus, causes agonising joint pain and raises the risk of stroke, heart attack and kidney disease. Current treatments, which range from steroids to immunosuppressants and targeted biologics, often fail to control the disease. Some 10% to 15% of people with lupus die prematurely.

Brittan Kopittke, 27, who works for the University of North Carolina helping to counsel patients considering CAR-T, was diagnosed with lupus at age 22. SLE, which affects about 300,000 people in the US, typically develops between the ages of 15 and 44.

What began as a rash on her chest rapidly progressed to crippling joint pain, mouth sores and crushing fatigue. Steroids to reduce inflammation and the antimalarial drug hydroxychloroquine to tamp down antibodies attacking her healthy cells and tissues failed.
“My mouth sores were rampant. I was struggling to eat. I was struggling to drink. I was just very, very miserable,” she said.
Despite trying a cocktail of medicines, her disease advanced, attacking her kidneys, heart and lungs.
“I had reached the end of the line with treatments,” she said.

In June 2024, Kopittke went to UNC-Chapel Hill for a trial testing CAR-T, a personalised immunotherapy successfully used to treat blood cancers. It involves removing blood cells called T cells, genetically reengineering them to attack rogue immune cells, and reinfusing them with the aim of growing new, healthy immune cells.

Kopittke developed two dangerous reactions: cytokine release syndrome, which causes systemic inflammation, and a life-threatening, high-grade neurological complication called ICANS that left her unresponsive for three days.

articles.title: Milking power: On the overturning of Gokul Dairy cooperative mandate
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Amid a nationwide outcry over electoral malpractices, with fresh evidence emerging every day, the BJP government in Maharashtra has gone a step further in overturning a popular mandate through an executive fiat. It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.

The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

It approved changing the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act through an ordinance on November 4 — which the Governor promulgated on November 6 — with the immediate effect of facilitating the takeover of the Kolhapur District Cooperative Milk Producers’ Union, popularly known as Gokul Dairy , by the BJP and its allies. A Congress-led panel won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the board of the cooperative on October 19. Gokul, which is one of Maharashtra’s most influential cooperative institutions, has an annual turnover of around ₹4,000 crore and is linked to several lakh milk producers in western Maharashtra. The BJP had set its eyes on the cooperative sector as yet another arena of its political dominance, creating a Ministry of Cooperation under Home Minister Amit Shah. While that plan of controlling cooperatives continues to play out through various means, the overturning of an election clearly won by the Congress-led Opposition marks a new level of brazenness by the BJP, and of the impunity its actions continue to receive from the judiciary.
• The Congress-backed Rajarshi Shahu Shetkari Samvichari Aghadi, led by Satej Patil, won 13 of the 25 elected seats on the Gokul board. On October 29, the election of the chairman was deadlocked after the BJP-allied members did not participate, and the meeting fell short of the required quorum of 14 members. The directors allied to the Congress and its partners subsequently declared Shashikant Patil Chuyekar as chairman, but the administration refused to recognise the election as quorum requirements had not been met. The amendment made through the ordinance allowed the government to nominate five directors to certain large cooperative institutions, with four nominees receiving voting rights. To be sure, four were nominated immediately to the Gokul board, and they voted with the BJP and its partners to elect a chairman on November 10 . The mandate of the cooperative’s members had been 13-12 in favour of the Congress and its allies, but it turned 16-13 in favour of the BJP and its partners, with the appointment of members with voting rights by the State government. Those defeated approached the Bombay High Court on November 9 to restrain the government-nominated directors from voting, but the High Court did not grant that relief. The diffidence of the judiciary in intervening in favour of democratic principles is turning out to be a matter of concern . The overturning of the popular mandate in Gokul Dairy cannot be seen as an isolated incident. It is yet another instance in a troubling pattern of state power silencing the people’s choice.

articles.title: Visions of the future: On this year’s Booker Prize
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: A defining feature of the world today is that knowledge is proliferating and societies are struggling to agree on what is happening. AI models have significantly catalysed this devolution, allowing bad actors to flood spaces ranging from the research literature to public airwaves with questionable information, and drawing the attention of governments worldwide to the security implications of such a potent technology. The Booker Prize for M. John Harrison’s The End of Everything , a novel about a sense-defying alien invasion and the unsettling prospect of un-understandability it confronts humans with, effectively acknowledges the centrality of the AI question both through the book’s substance and the judges’ choice. A consequence of rampant AI use has been an assault on people’s attention span as well as the ability to make sense of new claims, so much so that reliable, verifiable meaning has become a premium entity. The novel, on the other hand, attempts to diagnose a post-meaning world in which people are only left to look inward. The Prize is also a long-overdue victory for the merits of science fiction, a genre that Harrison helped shape from the late 1960s, and one that English literature’s top honours have repeatedly overlooked. That said, the novel itself is far from being its best example, including because Harrison’s diagnosis lets technology and the practice of power off the hook for their failures.

One of the judges said she had also sought a book “only a human being could write”, but defending a novel for its ability to thumb its nose at the machines is unfair to the literary enterprise and betrays a wider public anxiety about AI, especially over the lack of consensus about its proper place in society. OpenAI has been aggravating these deliberations among mathematicians by using its machines to make headway, in record time, on problems that have been unsolved for decades, without also contributing to mathematical education and research. Anthropic , the American company known for its Claude AI model, has announced its IPO with a surprising proposed valuation of $1.4 trillion . Since much of this is pegged on speculative future demand for AI services, the same absence of consensus leaves room for investors to imagine an enormous market for Anthropic’s products and invest to help the company realise them, thus narrowing the space for society to deliberate on all competing visions of the future. And while The End of Everything , with its philosophy of pragmatic absurdism, offers poor guidance on how to keep that space open, doing so ultimately remains one of the most important unfinished tasks before the world today.

articles.title: Caste and class: On OBC reservation
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: If public resources are to dismantle both caste hierarchy and class inequality, OBC reservation should resist the notion that caste disadvantage makes economic differences among OBC families irrelevant. The ‘creamy layer’ rules are responsible for identifying those OBC members who have advanced sufficiently to no longer require affirmative action. However, the government has implemented them inconsistently. The Supreme Court in March corrected one inconsistency, that the government cannot hold the salary alone of an OBC candidate’s parent as evidence of social advancement. In Indra Sawhney (1992) , the Court upheld the government’s 27% reservation for OBC candidates in central government services if it also excluded economically advanced sections, i.e., the creamy layer, among OBCs. Following the equivalence requirement issued in 1993, the Department of Personnel & Training (DoPT) issued a “clarification” in 2004 that the government used, from around 2015, to deny dozens of OBC candidates who had cleared the Civil Services Examination their benefits because their parents’ salaries exceeded the official threshold due to pay revisions that did not always reflect changes in occupational status. The Cabinet also approved equivalence guidelines in 2017 but a parliamentary committee criticised it over a number of issues.

In Rohith Nathan (2026) , the Court rightly rejected the government’s use of the 2004 “clarification” to arbitrarily exclude OBC candidates based on their parents’ salaries alone. However, the government stalled service allocations following the 2025 examination and appealed that retrospectively applying the ruling would create administrative chaos. On November 6, the Court conceded that it had not asked the government to reopen completed selections, as it could set workers against one another while leaving government misapplication unaddressed. A proactive policy is essential now as the government must create supernumerary posts for legitimate claimants and apply the 1993 rules to pending allocations without vouchsafing these remedies for only those who can afford litigation. Access to public employment continues to be grossly unequal: per the 2024-25 DoPT Annual Report, OBC representation in central government employment was 26.3% but declined steadily towards higher positions. As the Justice G. Rohini Commission also indicated, the benefits of reservation are distributed unevenly among OBC communities. However, the report, submitted in 2023, is still not in the public domain. The coming Census includes caste enumeration but policymakers also need data on each caste’s education, occupations, assets, and landholdings. Defending redistribution among caste groups while ignoring major inequalities within them, and constraining OBC reservation assuming relatively more high-income families capture the benefits without first establishing the extent and the causes are equally difficult to justify.

articles.title: Without any rationale: On the disbanding of the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: By abruptly disbanding the Justice Kurian Joseph Committee on Union-State Relations and handing over its task to the Tamil Nadu State Law Commission, the C. Joseph Vijay government appears to have succumbed to the political impulse to reverse earlier decisions rather than being guided by any compelling rationale or necessity. This gains credence from the very grounds cited. The committee executed its mandate with scholarly rigour, seen in Part I of its report that was submitted to the then M.K. Stalin government in February. Citing the Committee’s basic character of being a “non-statutory body” is unconvincing, particularly when the Law Commission itself is established only through “executive order”. There is also no public evidence of State Law Commissions having examined or addressed issues concerning Union-State relations. The mandate “to suggest ways and means for the inter-State relations and Centre-State relations”, constitutes only one part of the broader terms of reference of the State Law Commission, reconstituted in August. Given the commission’s wider responsibilities, successive State governments had constituted high-level committees to examine conflicts involving Concurrent List subjects and recommend specific remedies. It is through such recommendations that Tamil Nadu enacted certain pieces of legislation to overcome limitations imposed by central laws, including the provision of horizontal reservation in professional course admissions for disadvantaged students. Therefore, the State’s other argument of “similarity or overlap” in the “nature and scope of the functions” entrusted to the Committee and the Commission, does not withstand close scrutiny.

In September, Leader of the Opposition Udhayanidhi Stalin, had flagged an attempt to “paralyse” the Committee’s functioning . A fair assessment of the Committee’s Part I Report reveals the breadth and depth of its dispassionate examination of issues, including State autonomy, delimitation, and the office of the Governor. Parties, barring the BJP, had largely welcomed the report. Interestingly, its contents are not even remotely at odds with the broad public ideological positioning of Mr. Vijay’s Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam on State rights. Besides, Prof. M. Naganathan, the Committee’s only member with an overt political association, had already resigned. The government would do well to rethink and allow it to complete its work. This would strengthen the political endeavour towards evolving a more balanced federal governance structure, facilitating harmonious Centre-State relations.

articles.title: Cracker conundrum: On need for strict enforcement of cracker ban
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: The two Deepavali nights following the Supreme Court’s (SC) temporary relaxation of the cracker ban , played out predictably. The Air Quality Index (AQI) in several north Indian cities — already ‘poor’ and ‘very poor’ in the first week of November — was ‘severe’ on Deepavali night . Several air sensors — maintained by various organisations — reported PM2.5 in Delhi and its outskirts, exceeding 1,000 by Deepavali night. In this context, the SC’s order last week regarding crackers bears revisiting. While stating it was aware of the consequences of emissions from crackers, the Court has been waiting for quantitative evidence on the health and environmental effects of emissions from Deepavali celebrations. Such direct, causative evidence is almost impossible to furnish. Slackening winds and post-monsoon atmospheric dryness are known to trap the latent particulate matter from vehicles, industries, construction dust and stubble burning. Crackers are only an additional element that further degrades an already vitiated air. Delhi’s five-day average AQI rose from approximately 298 before Deepavali to 358 afterwards in 2024, 259 to 315 in 2025 and from 350 to 376 in 2026. While the timing of these spikes is consistent with a contribution from firecrackers, their precise share of overall pollution cannot be isolated from other emissions and meteorological influences. An absolute ban would encourage “illegal crackers from across the border,” the Court was told. Cracker season begins a fortnight before Deepavali and therefore an earlier decision by the Court regarding its permissibility would have given stockists time to better dispense ‘green’ crackers.

However, it is important to note that CSIR-NEERI, the developers of the products, underline that low-emission crackers — under stringent lab conditions — only reduce emissions by 30%–45%. These percentage reductions reveal nothing about gross particulate matter emissions. The post-Deepavali AQI is evidence of this. The Court acknowledges, but does not address, the immense implementation challenges in policing cracker sales and hyphenates crackers with religious observation but pays only lip service to provisions in the Constitution that say that religious customs cannot override considerations of health and life. Rather than wait for the week running up to Deepavali 2027, the Court must pronounce a final view on crackers and lay down the contours for the government to evolve a policy on limiting the manufacture, sale, and burning of crackers in a time-bound manner.

articles.title: Point of no return: On Israel’s next government
articles.examRelevance: UPSC & State PSC Mains / Essay: Deep Analytical Core Summary & Vocabulary
fullParagraphs: Israeli President Isaac Herzog’s decision to invite opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the next government reflects the real mandate of the October 27 legislative elections. While Mr. Eisenkot’s centrist Yashar party finished second with 21 seats, behind Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s Likud, which won 27, the former military chief, who campaigned on an anti-Netanyahu platform, has secured the support of 67 legislators in the 120-member Knesset. In Mr. Eisenkot’s own words, Israel risks “descending to dark places, to a point of no return”. But it is not yet clear what kind of a government Mr. Eisenkot is seeking to form. The opposition parties are split between a Jewish-led bloc with 48 MKs and an Arab-led bloc of 19 MKs. Arab parties have offered in-principle support for Mr. Eisenkot to keep Mr. Netanyahu’s right-religious coalition out of power. But what is not clear is whether they would be part of the government or offer outside support by allowing Mr. Eisenkot to run a minority government. Some of Mr. Eisenkot’s Jewish right-wing allies, such as Avigdor Lieberman, are opposed to joining hands with Arab parties. Mr. Eisenkot has now called for a unity government, appealing even to Likud and the far-right Religious Zionism, to join him.

But the challenges facing Israel’s next leader are formidable and immediate. Mr. Netanyahu’s unchecked militarism has deepened Israel’s international isolation, strained its relationship with the U.S., its most important patron and ally, and aggravated the security challenges it faces in its neighbourhood. At home, the surge of the far-right has further polarised society, while systemic violence against Palestinians has spread across the West Bank. Mr. Netanyahu’s response to these challenges has been to unleash more violence, which has only compounded Israel’s problems. If Mr. Eisenkot is serious about pulling Israel back from the point of no return, he must pursue a three-pronged approach. Firstly, he should form an Arab-Jewish unity government focused on healing the country’s internal wounds and bridging gaps between communities. Second, Israel’s deepening international isolation and increasingly negative public opinion around the world will begin to exact a heavy toll sooner rather than later. Tel Aviv must take urgent steps to restore its international standing. Third, Israel must reopen the path to peace. The new government should initiate negotiations with the Palestinians under international mediation, crack down on settler violence, pull back from Gaza and reaffirm its commitment to the two-state solution. Without peace, Israel risks continuing to “descend to dark places”.

articles.title: GAIL proposes ₹123-crore waste-to-biogas plant at KCDC site in Bengaluru
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL) has proposed setting up a 300-tonne-per-day (TPD) municipal solid waste-based compressed biogas (CBG) plant at the Karnataka Compost Development Corporation (KCDC) premises in Bengaluru. The project is estimated to cost ₹123.42 crore.

The proposed facility, spread across approximately 18 acres, will process 300 tonnes of segregated organic municipal waste daily to produce 12.6 tonnes of CBG and 21.6 tonnes of fermented organic manure (FOM) every day.
An awareness session on the project was organised on Wednesday. The biogas produced at the facility will be supplied to GAIL Gas, a wholly owned subsidiary of GAIL, for distribution as clean fuel.

According to GAIL, the plant is expected to reduce dependence on landfill disposal and provide a sustainable solution for processing the city’s organic waste. It will also have odour-control and effluent-treatment systems to minimise environmental impact.

The project is taken up as part of efforts to strengthen Karnataka’s waste-management infrastructure, aimed at promoting a circular economy by converting municipal waste into clean energy and organic manure.

articles.title: Police trap train jewellery thief through digital forensics
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Kerala Police and Railway Protection Force (RPF) have arrested a 38-year-old social media influencer from Tamil Nadu for stealing 47 sovereigns of gold jewellery from a 66-year-old woman aboard the Chennai-Thiruvananthapuram Mail. The accused, Balamurugan, was traced to his rented house in Coimbatore after a week-long investigation involving the examination of nearly 600 CCTV recordings.

The theft took place on November 3 when Kumari, 66, travelling in a reserved coach, found that the gold ornaments kept under her berth were missing. She had saved the jewellery for her granddaughter’s wedding. The police have recovered 36.42 sovereigns of the stolen gold.

After the theft, Balamurugan allegedly switched trains between Chennai and Salem before reaching Palakkad to avoid digital tracking. He got off at Palakkad railway station, took an autorickshaw to the KSRTC bus stand and travelled in five different buses to mislead the police. He also wore a mask, changed clothes and covered his forehead with his hands whenever he spotted surveillance cameras.

The breakthrough came when the police examined people seen wearing masks near Palakkad railway station around the time of the theft. A list of 10 suspects was prepared and narrowed down to five before Balamurugan was identified.

A special team of the State police, RPF and cyber experts used digital forensics, social media analysis, location tracking, financial transaction records and nearly 600 surveillance camera recordings to trace him to Coimbatore.

The investigation revealed that Balamurugan had acted in films and short films and was skilled in video editing. He also had a large social media following and reportedly led a lavish lifestyle. He had earlier spent around 40 days in jail in connection with the theft of a passenger’s laptop on a train in Madurai.

Police sources said that they suspected him to be a key member of an interstate gang targeting train passengers’ luggage. The operation was conducted under the supervision of Railway SP R. Krishnakumar and RPF Divisional Security Commissioner Ambu P. Kumar. RPF DySP Manoj, assistant security commissioner Anil, inspector A. Prathap and personnel from the RPF and its Crime Intelligence Branch were part of the investigation team.

articles.title: State spends Rs 1.85 lakh crore on guarantee schemes: H.M. Revanna
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: H.M. Revanna, chairman, Karnataka State Guarantee Schemes Implementation Authority on Wednesday said the State government has spent ₹1.85 lakh crore on the five guarantee schemes, accounting for 12% of the State budget.

Speaking after a meeting on the formation of guarantee committees at the gram panchayats and ward levels at the Zilla Panchayat office, Mr. Revanna said the benefits of the guarantee schemes reached beneficiaries directly without the involvement of middlemen or payment of bribes.

The schemes benefited eligible beneficiaries irrespective of caste. Each family received benefits worth around ₹5,000 to ₹6,000 under the guarantee schemes. Despite criticism in the initial days, the five guarantee schemes had continued to reach beneficiaries, he said.

Referring to the views of several economists on the schemes, Mr. Revanna said Karnataka ranked top among the States with the highest per capita income. The Gruha Lakshmi scheme had empowered women economically, he added.

He directed the taluk-level chairpersons of the guarantee scheme committees to take an active role in constituting village- and ward-level guarantee implementation committees, each comprising six members, including two women.
Authority vice-chairperson Pushpa Amarnath said that the lists of members for the gram panchayat- and ward-level guarantee committees would be prepared in two days and submitted to the State office.

District Committee president Arun Kumar said that 15,724 beneficiaries registered under the five guarantee schemes had died. Of these, 7,778 families of beneficiaries had applied for a change of beneficiary, nominating the woman head of the family, and were found eligible, he said.

Following the death of a beneficiary, eligible family members can continue to avail the benefits under the five guarantee schemes by nominating the eldest woman in the family as the beneficiary, he added.

Shivkumar, vice-president of the District Guarantee Scheme Implementation Committee said the Food and Civil Supplies Department should take the initiative to issue BPL cards on priority to people suffering from serious health conditions.

Beneficiaries facing technical difficulties while withdrawing money from banks were brought to the notice of the district committee president during the meeting. It was suggested to direct bank managers to address their grievances.

articles.title: Bengaluru police arrest 34 in citywide drug crackdown; narcotics worth ₹12.61 crore seized
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: The Bengaluru City Police have arrested 34 people, including two foreign nationals and nine persons from other States, in a major crackdown on drug trafficking across 11 police station limits. Narcotic substances with an estimated market value of ₹12.61 crore were seized during the operation.

The seized drugs include 5.519 kg of MDMA, 46.486 kg of ganja, 72.82 grams of cocaine and 1.542 litres of hashish oil. The police also seized eight mobile phones, two two-wheelers and ₹1,000 in cash. The value of the seized narcotics were estimated to be worth ₹6.30 crore at procurement prices.
The raids were conducted in the jurisdictions of Hebbal, Koramangala, D.J. Halli, Mahalakshmi Layout, Yeshwanthpur, Adugodi, Hennur, Govindapura, Begur, Hebbagodi and Bandepalya police stations.

According to the police, the operation followed specific inputs from informants about the sale of banned narcotic substances in these areas. Cases were registered under the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act before conducting raids at the identified locations.

During interrogation, the accused allegedly revealed that they procured drugs at lower prices from suppliers in the State, abroad and other States, and sold them at higher prices to people, including college students, for quick profits.

The police are now investigating the supply chain to identify the suppliers and uncover the wider drug distribution network. All 34 accused have been produced before the jurisdictional courts and remanded to judicial custody.

articles.title: IMOP opens second manufacturing facility at Sri City
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: Japanese steel processing joint-venture company India Metal One Steel Plate Processing Private Limited (IMOP) opened its second manufacturing facility strengthening its 15-year-old partnership with Sri City. The new plant, spread across 12,000 square metres, involves an investment of ₹108 crore, taking IMOP’s total investment in Sri City to ₹408 crore.

The new facility is expected to increase its annual production capacity by 25 per cent — from 48,000 million tonnes (MT) to 60,000 MT — and to create 200 additional jobs, taking the total workforce to 850 employees.

IMOP managing director Taizo Iwami expressed hope that the new facility would enhance the company’s deliverability of high-quality products by helping it adhere to the highest standards of safety and timely service.

Sri City managing director Ravindra Sannareddy, while congratulating the IMOP team, called the expansion a testament to the confidence of global investors in Sri City. He also appreciated the company for contributing to social development in the vicinity through CSR funds.

The inaugural ceremony was attended by Metal One Corporation’s executive officer and chief operating officer (COO) Masashi Mizuno, Metal One India’s chairman and managing director Yikita Sato among others.

On the occasion, Mr. Iwami presented awards to long-standing business partners such as Caterpillar, Kobelco, Tata-Hitachi and Doosan Bobcat, in addition to its supplier partners such as Tata Steel, Jindal Steel and JSW Steel.

articles.title: Chittoor, Annamayya mango growers fear dry spell, rainfall deficit likely to impact 2027 yields
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II: Polity, Governance, Supreme Court Judgements, Bills & Govt Schemes
fullParagraphs: A harsh dry spell and severe rainfall shortages due to El Niño conditions have put the mango orchards across Chittoor and Annamayya districts in serious crisis as farmers prepare their trees for the upcoming flowering season. With the soil rapidly drying and local water tables under immense pressure, mango growers fear that the prolonged dry spell will wreck the 2027 season’s blooms, fruit set, and overall yields.

The numbers behind the rainfall deficit are alarming. Chittoor received only 445.7 mm of rain against its usual 677 mm — a 34.2% shortfall. Meanwhile, in Annamayya district, the situation is even distraught, with just 302.5 mm recorded against a normal 574 mm, with a 47.3% deficit.

Chittoor district alone has roughly 51,736 hectares planted with Totapuri mangoes, boasting an expected production capacity of 5.17 lakh tonnes. Considering the wider belt spanning Chittoor, Tirupati, Annamayya, and Kadapa, Totapuri cultivation stretches across nearly 90,000 hectares, with close to 50,000 farmers involved and producing an estimated 9 lakh tonnes every year.

The major mago growing hubs include Bangarupalem, Puthalapattu, Aragonda, Thavanampalle, Puttur, and Palamaner in Chittoor district; Rayachoti and Rajampet in Annamayya district, and Railway Koduru in Tirupati district respectively.

Kothur Babu, the president of the Chittoor District Mango Producers’ Association, said that traditional mango farming follows a rigid calendar. Once the May-August harvest wraps up, farmers immediately dive into pruning, cleaning up orchards, applying manure, and managing whatever irrigation they have left. Flowering usually gets rolling between December and February, paving the way for pollination and fruit setting.
“Though a bit of dry weather is actually necessary right before flowering kicks off, severe and prolonged water stress starves the trees and stops uniform blooms from happening,” he said.

Chittoor is a vibrant centre for mango pulp production as thousands of local processing unit workers, drivers, and transporters rely on a steady stream of the harvested fruit. “If this intense water crunch continues, Chittoor could easily see a 10 per cent to 20 per cent drop from its usual 5.17 lakh tonnes. The production loss could be more than one lakh tonnes in 2027,” said a Horticulture Department official in Annamayya district.
Meanwhile, mango growers said they desperately need rain over the next few weeks to save their trees and protect the traditional annual economy.

articles.title: Two days past Deepavali, NPCI yet to announce a date for UPI MDR rollout
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Two days since Deepavali, the National Payments Council of India is yet to notify a new date for the implementation of the Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on UPI transactions and The Hindu has learnt that “there is no announcement on this at the moment”.

When it had put the proposed additional charge on hold nearly a month ago, the NPCI had said the new date would be announced “immediately” after Deepavali. The new rate was originally supposed to have been implemented on October 15.
“There is no announcement on this at the moment,” a spokesperson at the NPCI told The Hindu when asked whether the NPCI’s date announcement was imminent.

The matter of an MDR levy on specified UPI transactions received significant pushback from merchants and petrol pump dealers alike, apart from customers who feared that merchants would pass on the extra charge on to them by way of higher prices.
The petrol pump dealers further said that the MDR charge, coupled with the fact that their dealer commission had not been revised in several years, meant that their margins would be further squeezed.

The NPCI had on October 13 announced that its UPI and Services Steering Committee had decided that “keeping in mind the festive season, Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) on select Person-to-Merchant (P2M) UPI transactions, shall be implemented immediately post Diwali at a date to be notified separately”.

The Hindu had at the time reported that, according to government sources, the decision to delay the implementation of MDR on UPI was made in the Prime Minister’s Office following strong appeals from traders.

Praveen Khandelwal, founder and secretary-general of the Confederation of All India Traders (CAIT) and a Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) Lok Sabha member, had welcomed the deferment, saying that it would protect traders’ interests and sustain digital payment momentum during the festive season.

articles.title: Moody’s ups India’s FY27 growth estimate to 7% on broad-based momentum
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Moody's Ratings on Wednesday (November 11, 2026) said the Indian economy is expected to grow at a higher rate of 7 per cent in the current fiscal, led by broad-based economic momentum and energy supply shock resilience.

In its Global Macro Outlook 2027-28, Moody's, however, said that near-term risks to growth persist as household consumption remains vulnerable to “intensifying and broadening price pressures”, with headline inflation close to the upper end of the Reserve Bank of India's (RBI) 2-6% target range, while a deficient southwest monsoon and strengthening El Nino conditions will weigh on agricultural output and rural demand.
“India's broad-based economic momentum and demonstrated resilience to the energy supply shock warrant upward revisions to our 2026-27 growth forecasts to 7% from 6.5%,” it said.
Robust consumption, improving investment dynamics and strong macroeconomic fundamentals imply that the economy appears well positioned to sustain growth near 7% over the medium term, Moody's said.
A sustained private investment boom that materially boosts manufacturing, employment and productivity could lift growth rates above Moody's baseline projections.
“With the RBI on track to raise rates further, tighter monetary policy could delay the recovery in private investment,” Moody's added.

India has adjusted to the energy price shock better than previously assumed, helped by its ability to diversify crude and gas supplies and buffer consumers from the immediate price impact through state-backed oil marketing companies and tax cuts.

India is also home to the world's largest single-site refining complex, and its large and sophisticated refining capacity has helped limit fuel supply disruptions while supporting its role as a major exporter of refined petroleum products, Moody's added.

“High frequency indicators, including robust capital goods production and imports, accelerating industrial credit growth and rising capacity utilisation, suggest that India may be at the cusp of a new private capex cycle after several years of corporate and banking- sector balance sheet repair,” the U.S.-based agency said.

Broader economic activity also remains solid amid expanding manufacturing and services purchasing manager indexes and double-digit year-on-year growth in goods and services tax revenue, vehicle sales and merchandise exports, it added.

articles.title: Industry seeks LTCG, STT cuts in Budget 2027; MSME relief also on wish list
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: Several industry bodies have recommended to the Ministry of Finance that the upcoming Budget 2027 should rationalise the Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on equities and reduce the rate of the Securities Transaction Tax (STT).

Officials in the Finance Ministry, including Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and Revenue Secretary Arvind Shrivastava, have been conducting their pre-Budget consultative meetings, during which they met the Confederation of Indian Industry (CII), Federation of Indian Chambers of Commerce and Industry (FICCI), the PHD Chamber of Commerce and Industry (PHDCCI), and the Associated Chambers of Commerce and Industry (ASSOCHAM), among others.

One of the most-cited requests from the industry was the rationalisation of LTCG on equities. In Budget 2026, the Centre removed the 12.5% LTCG tax in the government securities market for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) alongside other measures including reforms under the Fully Accessible Route (FAR).

Currently, foreign and domestic investors have to pay 12.5% tax on the sale of equities on gains exceeding Rs 1.25 lakh per annum on listed shares. The Centre has held several meetings with the Securities and Exchange Board of India, the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) and other industry players.

“Removing the LTCG levy would raise post-tax returns and close a gap with Korea, Taiwan and Brazil,” Rakesh Nangia, chairman of task force on International Taxes at ASSOCHAM said. “The debt market is a useful precedent, which after the G-sec relief, saw FPI inflows rise to about $9 billion in June-July.”

The PHDCCI has requested that the government abolish LTCG tax on equity investments, reduce the short-term capital gains (STCG) tax rate from 20% to 10%, and lower STT rates “to encourage long-term investment and improve India’s capital market competitiveness”.

In its representation to Ms. Sitharaman, FICCI highlighted the fact that foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) have withdrawn about Rs 3.08 lakh crore during the year. It added that capital gains tax, which is charged over and above the STT, erodes returns from equities, and needs a review to make India a more attractive place to invest.

However, other market players highlight that the revenue loss incurred from the removal of LTCG could be negated through a hike in STT. According to estimates by SBI Research, the removal of LTCG would result in a revenue loss of Rs 40,000-50,000 crore for FY28.

One of the key frictions for FPIs underscored by industry bodies and equity analysts is the computation of the tax. Under Income-Tax Act, the calculation of the LTCG is in the Indian rupee. The challenge arises due to currency depreciation as against the investor’s base currency during the holding period, due to which investors are still liable to pay tax even when net returns in dollar terms are flat or even negative. This issue is currently under examination.

VK Vijayakumar, chief investment strategist at Geojit Financial Services also cautioned against selective relief, noting that abolishing LTCG solely for FPIs would be discriminatory against domestic retail and direct equity investors who remain subject to the 12.5% tax. He urged any tax relief must apply equally across the board to ensure a level playing field.

Industry experts also suggest that while amendments in tax laws are just one part of attracting inflows, what remains important is continued momentum in corporate earnings growth, policy certainty and a stable rupee.

As such, simplifying onboarding and setting one predictable tax clearance process at exit coupled with making dispute resolution faster and binding is what would bring stable long-term investments, Nangia noted.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz LNG traffic hits highest in October since Iran war began
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The monthly tally of laden liquefied natural gas (LNG) tankers exiting the ​Strait of Hormuz reached its highest in October since ‌the U.S.-Iran conflict disrupted shipping this year, vessel ​tracking data showed.

* Last month, ⁠31 LNG tankers went through the key waterway, according to data from S&P Global Energy, of which ‌23 were loaded at Ras Laffan in Qatar and eight at Das Island ‌in the United Arab Emirates.
* October exports ‌were ⁠the highest since February when the war ⁠started and were up from September’s corresponding tally of 23 vessels exiting the strait, the data showed.
* “We are ​looking at UAE ‌back to pre-war transit levels and Qatar at over 30% of pre-war Hormuz transits,” said Eric Yep, a senior principal analyst at ‌S&P Global Energy.
* Kpler’s shiptracking data showed ​42 LNG cargoes were loaded in October, up from 27 in September.

* ⁠The changes come as Ras Laffan’s October loadings reached 35 cargoes, surpassing 2.7 million tons, the ‌highest since the war started, according to Kpler data. Qatar exported nearly 6.2 million tons in February.

* Two of the vessels carrying LNG from Ras Laffan that exited the strait subsequently conducted ship-to-ship (STS) transfers off the coast of ‌Oman’s Sohar anchorage, Kpler data showed. The SC Prestige ​transferred LNG to the BW ENN Crystal Sky, which is now bound for ⁠South Korea.
* The Al Mafyar moved its LNG ⁠to Shandong Redwood and Ejnan, both of which delivered the cargoes to Pakistan.
* ‌Das Island exports held steady at seven loadings in October, flat with September, Kpler ​data showed.

articles.title: RBI extends Abhyudaya Bank supersession by another year
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has extended the supersession of the board of Mumbai-based Abhyudaya Co-operative Bank Ltd. by another year, effective November 24, 2026, citing public interest.

“Upon a review, the Reserve Bank of India is satisfied that, in the public interest, it is necessary to further extend the period of supersession beyond the close of business of the bank as on November 23, 2026,” the RBI said in a circular.
The RBI first superseded the bank’s Board of Directors for one year on November 24, 2023, citing “material concerns arising from poor governance standards observed within the bank.”
The supersession, initially imposed for a year, has since been extended annually, first in November 2024, again in November 2025 and now for a further year from November 24, 2026.

With the latest extension, Mr. Satya Prakash Pathak will continue as the bank’s Administrator. He will be assisted by the existing Committee of Advisors comprising Mr. Venkatesh Hegde, Mr. Devendra Kumar and Mr. Suhas Gokhale.

articles.title: OALP deepwater bidding deadline extended again to December 10
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-III & Banking/SSC: RBI Monetary Policy, GDP, Inflation, Budget & Banking
fullParagraphs: The Directorate General of Hydrocarbons (DGH) on Monday extended the deadline for submitting bids for deepwater and ultra-deepwater blocks under the 10th and 11th rounds of the Open Acreage Licensing Policy (OALP) by 25 days to December 10.

The latest extension marks the seventh for the 10th round, launched in April last year, and the third for the 11th round, which opened in March this year. The deadlines were last extended in September by nearly two months to November 15.
The 10th round offers 25 blocks, including one deepwater and 12 ultra-deepwater blocks, while the 11th round has five blocks on offer, comprising one deepwater and four ultra-deepwater areas.

In August, the Union Cabinet approved an outlay of ₹84,084 crore for the Petroleum Ministry’s National Offshore Exploration Scheme, titled ‘Samudra Manthan’. The corpus, to be utilised until FY31, includes ₹43,200 crore for drilling 60 deepwater and ultra-deepwater wells.

State-owned explorers ONGC and Oil India have also announced substantial investments in offshore exploration. ONGC plans to invest ₹1 lakh crore by 2030, while Oil India has earmarked ₹15,000 crore over the next three years for deepwater and ultra-deepwater exploration.

articles.title: Netanyahu dismisses claims that Israel blocking supplies to Gaza
articles.examRelevance: GS Paper-II & Current Affairs: Bilateral Agreements, Foreign Visits & UN/G20/BRICS
fullParagraphs: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected accusations that Israel has been delaying the entry of winter supplies into the Gaza Strip as the enclave faces worsening conditions this week, with severe rains flooding makeshift tents.
He said Israel was not to blame for the worsening conditions for Palestinians in Gaza's tent camps that have been hit by severe winter floods.

His remarks came after the U.S.-created Board of Peace — established under U.S. President Donald Trump's plan to end the Israel-Hamas war and oversee Gaza's recovery — said Monday (November 9, 2026) that Israel's delaying of the entry of winter supplies into Gaza had “exacerbated the consequences of a foreseeable humanitarian challenge”.

Torrential rain has battered the war-torn enclave in recent days, damaging tens of thousands of makeshift tents. Four people, including three children, were killed on Sunday (November 8, 2026) when a large sandstone slab collapsed onto tents during the rains.

Mr. Netanyahu said the Palestinian militant group Hamas is to blame because it continues to refuse to disarm, a condition of the deal announced by Mr. Trump, and seizes humanitarian aid in order to use it for military purposes.
“Hamas alone is responsible for the suffering of the people of Gaza, and it is now cynically exploiting that suffering to shift blame onto Israel once again,” he said on Tuesday (November 10, 2026).

British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the situation in Gaza was “intolerable” and demanded Israel end “arbitrary restrictions” on aid. And in Washington, Senator Brian Schatz of Hawaii, the top Democrat on the Senate's foreign spending subcommittee, called for Israel to immediately allow winter gear into Gaza.

“There are a lot of challenges when it comes to Israel and Palestine that are complicated, and fraught, and contentious,” Mr. Schatz said on the Senate floor on Tuesday (November 10, 2026). “But we should all be able to agree that repairing torn tents and helping people to dry out, and providing warmth to freezing children is a basic human obligation.”
